articles.title: Cope Defends Roman Reigns and Comments on WWE Return, Heyman Addresses Brock Lesnar's Retirement
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.

Amid more commentary that Roman Reigns is overrated, one of his former WWE rivals stepped up to explain why the discussion annoys him.

Appearing on The Ariel Helwani Show , Copeland dismissed criticism of Reigns as being "subjective" before praising how "easy" and "fun" it was to work with him when they were paired up in WWE.

The discussion of Reigns has taken off in recent weeks with Eric Bischoff recently joining in by saying he's gotten bored with the OTC because "I don't see anything new from" him.

While it is fair to criticize WWE going back to The Bloodline well, it certainly doesn't appear like it's going to stick around as long as the first iteration did since Reigns was attacked by Solo Sikoa on Monday's episode of Raw.

As far as Reigns being overrated, he's been the clear top guy in WWE for six years and unquestionably a huge drawing card. It's not his fault the creative team has struggled to come up with younger stars who it can push at the same level.

Copeland and Reigns only shared the ring four times , but one of them was a WrestleMania main event triple-threat match that also included Daniel Bryan.

Sticking with Copeland and his career, the WWE Hall of Famer has no interest in going back to his old stomping grounds.

In the same Helwani interview (h/t Subhojeet Mukherjee of Ringside News), Copeland said in no uncertain terms he plans for AEW to be the final stop on his storied career.

"Yes. Yeah. That's where I want to. I know that may disappoint a lot of people, but I love it there. ... I love the company. I love the attitude, the exuberance. I love the drive. I love the excitement that I see from the locker room. Yeah, I don't wanna go anywhere else. I'm good. I did everything I could do there, and then some. And again, they got everything out of me that they could have. So it's for the better, which is all you can ask for in a partnership."

Copeland's contract is believed to expire at some point in 2027, though he admitted he's not even sure due to time added on for injuries and film projects.

Now at 52 years old, Copeland has had an incredible second act to his career after initially retiring in 2011 due to injuries. He returned to the ring at the 2020 Royal Rumble, spent three years in WWE before making the jump to AEW.

Copeland and Christian Cage won the AEW tag titles by defeating FTR in an I Quit match at Double or Nothing. They successfully defended their crown against the Dogs at Forbidden Door.

Next up for Cope and Cage is a showdown with the Young Bucks at All In from Wembley Stadium on Aug. 30.

Paul Heyman Talks Brock Lesnar's Retirement

Even though Brock Lesnar claimed to retire earlier this year with his first loss to Oba Femi at WrestleMania, it was his second declaration after SummerSlam that caught the attention of Paul Heyman.

Appearing on the Six Feet Under podcast with The Undertaker (h/t Mukherjee ), Heyman explained why Lesnar's tone this time around made him believe the retirement announcement is for real.

"But I knew that this was it," Heyman said. "Because he knew that this was it. He wasn't just saying it because he felt it at the moment."

Heyman noted in the past he would have discussions with Lesnar that indicated he was leaning toward retirement, but his tone would change as his contract came closer to expiring.

"I would hear this every year from him. 'Nope. This is my last contract. This is it.' And he meant it when he said it. ... As we got closer, he would then change his mind, or it didn't take a lot to talk him into it," said Heyman.

Lesnar revealed on the Aug. 4 episode of The Pat McAfee Show that he is retired from wrestling "and everything else too."

The announcement came three days after Lesnar was defeated by Femi on the first night of SummerSlam. Lesnar then cut an in-ring promo after the match declaring The Ruler to be the future of WWE.

There was immediate skepticism that Lesnar won't wrestle again, including some WWE officials reportedly believing he will perform at WrestleMania 43 next year in Saudi Arabia for a huge sum of money.

It wouldn't be a surprise after Lesnar seemingly retired at WrestleMania by leaving his boots and gloves in the ring only to return a month later.

articles.title: WWE WrestleMania 42 Attendance Revealed, How Big Was Drop from WM 41 That Set All-Time Gate Record?
articles.summary: Official numbers from the Las Vegas Stadium Authority show WrestleMania 42 attendance was down roughly 15 percent from the previous year.
articles.body:
Official numbers from the Las Vegas Stadium Authority show WrestleMania 42 attendance was down roughly 15 percent from the previous year.

The Las Vegas Stadium Authority announced the two-day attendance for this year's WrestleMania was 97,126 with the split being 47,093 on Saturday and 50,033 on Sunday.

WWE NXT Results, Winners, Live Grades, Reaction, Highlights Before Heatwave 2026

The attendance marks a drop of 21,515 from 2025, which was also the most financially successful pro wrestling show ever with a $66 million gate across the two nights.

WrestleMania 42 marks the first time since 2021, when attendance was still limited due to the COVID-19 pandemic, that WWE's marquee event did draw more than 100,000 fans for the two-night event.

Despite the drop in attendance, WWE and TKO have touted WrestleMania 42 as "one of the highest-grossing events in company history," including record or near-record figures across across gate, sponsorship, merchandise, WWE World, On Location VIP experiences and digital.

Last year's show was largely built around John Cena's heel turn and his chase to win a record-setting 17th world championship against Cody Rhodes. It was also Cena's first WrestleMania match since losing to Austin Theory in 2023.

WrestleMania 42 featured Rhodes defeating Randy Orton to retain the undisputed WWE title in the main event of night one and Roman Reigns beating CM Punk in the main event of night two to win the world heavyweight championship.

Next year's WrestleMania will be held in Saudi Arabia, marking the first time it has taken place outside of North America.

articles.title: Fantasy Football: 7 players Justin Boone thinks could be league winners in 2026
articles.summary: These players could define the 2026 fantasy football season.
articles.body:
Identifying the players who could define the fantasy season is one of my favorite exercises to do each year. While it's unlikely you'll be able to draft all the names on this list, building your roster around even a few of these players can significantly increase your odds of reaching the fantasy playoffs and hopefully bringing home the championship.

When it became obvious earlier this offseason that A.J. Brown's time with the Eagles was coming to an end, I didn't expect to be as interested in Hurts for fantasy. Usually, it's a bad omen when a quarterback loses their top receiver. However, the more I dug into Hurts' outlook moving forward, the more optimistic it turned out to be.

Even in a down season last year, Hurts still finished as the QB8 in fantasy points per game. That makes it five consecutive campaigns inside the top eight at his position, including finishes as the QB6, QB2, QB1 and QB7 overall.

While Hurts isn't without blame for Philly's struggles a year ago, we can easily point to former offensive coordinator Kevin Patullo's stagnant scheme as a big part of the problem. Enter new OC Sean Mannion, who will modernize their attack with more pre-snap motion and play-action. He's also challenging Hurts to evolve his game and take more chances downfield.

Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Football league for the 2026 NFL season

To do that, Hurts will need time in the pocket. Another factor that held the Eagles back last season was the health of their offensive line. Better injury luck is never guaranteed, but we can be hopeful their starters don't deal with as many ailments this time around. Brandon Thorn of Establish the Run ranked this group as the second best set of blockers in the league.

Replacing Brown in the passing game won't be easy, but DeVonta Smith has long been an overqualified No. 2 receiver. (Spoiler: we'll discuss him more a little further down this list.)

First-round wideout Makai Lemon has missed significant time with a hamstring injury, so his impact may not be truly felt until partway through the season. Fortunately, Dontayvion Wicks has stepped up and appears to be ready for a meaningful role with his new club. That doesn't even account for superstar back Saquon Barkley and stalwart tight end Dallas Goedert.

If you're still not convinced, know that Hurts will encounter the easiest fantasy schedule of any quarterback — a major improvement from what he faced last year.

Thanks to all the talented fantasy options among quarterbacks this season, Hurts is going off the board as the QB6 near the Round 5-6 turn. I've even seen him fall to the seventh round in some of my redraft leagues this month. That's incredible value for a player who always has the potential for a transcendent season — aided by his tush-push-inflated TD scoring.

Some of my favorite builds this summer have involved me drafting two running backs, two receivers and a tight end in the first five rounds, before grabbing Hurts in the sixth or seventh.

Taylor represents a very specific range in drafts, since he's almost always gone inside the top seven selections of the first round. It's an area where you want to come away with a player who can be the anchor of your fantasy lineup and we saw JT accomplish that feat last season.

While he ended the year as the second-highest scoring running back (20.9 fppg) behind only Christian McCaffrey, that included the games where Philip Rivers and Riley Leonard had to step in for an injured Daniel Jones down the stretch.

Before Jones got hurt, Taylor was the RB1 overall with 23 fppg in half PPR — ahead of CMC — through the first 13 weeks. He was also averaging 104 rushing yards per contest during that span. With Jones on the field the Colts were No. 1 in yards per play, EPA per play, success rate and points per drive. After his injury they failed to win a game and fell to 18th or worse in all those categories. Taylor dropped to just 57 yards per outing.

Even if Jones isn't 100% back to form for Week 1, having him under center will be a big boost to the offense. With him, Taylor can challenge for elite status among fantasy RBs as he goes up against the seventh easiest collection of opponents for his position in 2026, while running behind an offensive line the aforementioned Brandon Thorn ranked sixth best league-wide.

It's also safe to wonder if we could witness another career high in receptions for Taylor, after he posted 46 last year. With Michael Pittman Jr. gone and Alec Pierce dealing with an ankle injury that could sideline him at the beginning of the season, Taylor might be relied upon even more as a pass-catcher.

Few players have the talent and volume to compete for the fantasy RB crown, but Taylor is among them.

Walker occupied this same space last year and began the season with two top-10 weekly RB finishes in the first three weeks, but ultimately spent most of the season splitting time with Zach Charbonnet. The Seahawks' decision to split backfield touches turned out to be the right one because it kept Walker fresh for a late-season run that helped them win the Super Bowl.

Over Walker's final six games (including three playoff contests), he averaged 128.5 scrimmage yards and nearly a touchdown per appearance. Those numbers were amplified by Charbonnet suffering a torn ACL in the postseason, but Walker's hot streak had already begun by that point. It eventually culminated in taking home the Super Bowl MVP award.

Though that hindsight analysis can't change our 2025 fantasy results, there's plenty of reason to get excited about Walker's potential this season.

Walker ended up in one of the ideal landing spots for a running back, joining a Chiefs offense that's been in desperate need of a playmaker who could elevate its ground attack.

The 25-year-old (turns 26 in October) is finally escaping the timeshare backfield in Seattle and won't face anywhere near the same competition for touches in Kansas City. By all accounts the Chiefs want to deploy Walker as a workhorse and help take some of the pressure off their passing attack.

While I don't expect him to ever catch enough passes to flirt with an elite season-long finish at his position, this move definitely puts him in consideration as a top-five fantasy RB — as long as he can stay healthy.

Whether it's Walker, Chase Brown or Omarion Hampton, the running backs in the second round of fantasy drafts offer tremendous value this year.

Smith has played in A.J. Brown's shadow for a long time, so it's nice to see him getting an opportunity to prove he can be a No. 1 receiver in the NFL.

Fortunately, we've been given a glimpse of what that might look like already. Over the last two seasons, there have been three games where Brown was sidelined and Smith played a full complement of snaps. The results were stat lines of 6-84-0, 7-79-0 and 7-76-1 while averaging just under 10 targets per game.

It's not like Smith has been invisible with Brown on the field. Smith was the WR17 (2024), WR21 (2023) and WR16 (2022) on a per game basis, before this past season when he finished as the WR33 amid some overall struggles in the Eagles' offense.

As I outlined in Jalen Hurts' section, there are plenty of signs pointing to the Eagles having a bounce-back campaign, including their new coordinator, some better offensive health and a very soft schedule. Like Hurts, Smith also will enjoy the easiest slate at his position in 2026.

The 27-year-old (turns 28 in November) is more than capable of shining in a bigger role and with Makai Lemon battling hamstring issues, there won't be anyone around to challenge him for the top spot.

Don't be surprised when Smith finishes as a low-end fantasy WR1 this season.

The annual tradition of trying to uncover this season's version of last year's meaningful fantasy stars can often lead managers astray as they attempt to force comparisons.

However, this year we definitely have a clear candidate to be this season's George Pickens — and that's Waddle.

Pickens was a talented receiver who flashed high-end skills in a low-volume Steelers' passing attack with questionable quarterback play. Then he joined the Cowboys high-volume pass game, where he instantly got an upgrade at QB in Dak Prescott. Though a CeeDee Lamb injury certainly helped his fantasy cause, Pickens finished as the WR6 in fppg in his debut season in Dallas.

Now consider Waddle's situation. It's been a couple seasons since he was a true impact fantasy starter, but he still managed WR28 stats on a struggling Dolphins team last year.

If you look back to the early part of his career in Miami, Waddle produced over 1,000 yards in each of his first three campaigns, resulting in fantasy finishes of WR17, WR11 and WR22.

The Broncos paid a premium to acquire Waddle, including a first-round pick, which is a sign they view him as a key piece of their offense moving forward.

So we have a talented wideout in his prime (turns 28 in November) going to a quality offense with a better quarterback where he'll be featured as the No. 1 receiver. There's no need for an injury to open things up the way it did for Pickens in Dallas.

On top of being Bo Nix's favorite target moving forward, Waddle will get an increase in targets from Denver's high-volume approach through the air. The Broncos had the fourth most pass attempts (613) in 2025, versus the Dolphins who were third lowest in that category (479).

I'm expecting Waddle to be one of the players fantasy managers look back at after the season and wish they drafted more.

Washington being highlighted in this section shouldn't shock anyone, since it's only the millionth time I've written or spoken about him in recent months.

Maybe I'm just trying to match the number of positive quotes that have come out of Jacksonville from coaches, teammates and beat writers, who are all indicating Washington will be the team's No. 1 receiver.

Sometimes we can travel down a misleading path when we get too caught up in partial-season stats. But the combination of Washington's strong finish in 2025 and the overwhelming praise he's getting this offseason are impossible to ignore.

Following the Jaguars' Week 8 bye, it was Washington who led the receiver room the rest of the way, putting up 90 yards and/or a touchdown in five of his last seven games. That even included a Week 13 contest where he left early due to a hip strain.

Washington was the WR19 in fppg over the final nine weeks of the fantasy season, ahead of Jakobi Meyers (WR31) who joined the team in a midseason trade and Brian Thomas Jr. (WR44) who failed to recapture the magic of his rookie campaign. First-rounder Travis Hunter was injured midseason and now projects to be a part-time offensive weapon while taking on a larger role on defense.

You can disregard the consistent drumbeat around Washington if you want, but I'm leaning all the way in on this one, as Jacksonville's wideouts prepare to face the sixth easiest fantasy schedule in 2026.

Even if he can't match his top-20 production down the stretch, Washington has a defined path to WR3 numbers — which is exactly where he's being drafted.

Normally, my approach to drafting a fantasy tight end involves grabbing an elite option or waiting to find a value much later. However, I've made an exception when it comes to Warren because he's an elite fantasy TE whom you can get one, two or sometimes three rounds later than the top trio at the position.

As a rookie, Warren broke onto the fantasy scene as the TE6 in per game scoring through Week 10, before he dealt with injuries down the stretch and lost his starting quarterback Daniel Jones.

On the season, Warren led the team in targets with 112, one more than teammate Michael Pittman Jr., who joined the Steelers this offseason. Alec Pierce's recovery from ankle surgery is ongoing and might result in him missing time at the start of the season. Even when Pierce is active, he's far from a target hog.

Josh Downs and Keenan Allen will benefit from the situation as well, but there's a real opportunity for the sophomore tight end to dominate targets on the Colts this year.

Jones is back and looking ready to start in Week 1. Whether he maintains his mobility coming off a torn Achilles is another question and could lead to more quick passing to the short-to-intermediate ranges of the field, where Warren excels.

His yards after the catch ability is also worth noting. Warren was second among all tight ends in total yards after the catch behind only Trey McBride. Warren was 13th in the league in YAC among all positions.

The 24-year-old's fantasy numbers can even be boosted by occasional deployment from the backfield. That was part of his game in college and he earned six carries last season, even scoring a touchdown on the ground.

Warren has a lot of the things we're looking for in an elite fantasy tight end, especially the potential to lead his team in targets and add value after the catch. Consider him Brock Bowers-lite, with an outside chance to compete for the TE1 overall throne.

articles.title: Pat McAfee Sounds Off on WWE Future in New Video After Randy Orton's WrestleMania 42 Loss
articles.summary: Pat McAfee is seemingly cutting ties with WWE after Randy Orton's loss at WrestleMania 42.
articles.body:
Pat McAfee is seemingly cutting ties with WWE after Randy Orton's loss at WrestleMania 42.

The ESPN personality said that fans shouldn't expect to see him in WWE programming "ever again."

"I made a promise that I would never, ever be seen on WWE television ever again," McAfee said. "And Cody Rhodes won. He is the one. Wow. What a dog he turned out to be. Maybe he was the right one all along… Wrestling fans can sleep soundly understanding I will never be back over there."

Ahead of WrestleMania, McAfee was revealed as Orton's mystery ally for "The Viper's" match against Cody Rhodes, and he said he wouldn't return to WWE if Orton lost the match.

Ultimately, Rhodes won and retained his undisputed WWE championship.

McAfee, a punter for the Indianapolis Colts from 2009 to 2016, got involved with WWE during his playing career and began to appear more often once he retired. He later started commentating for WWE matches, with his most recent appearance being at WrestleMania in April.

He also said on his ESPN talk show after WrestleMania that he had no plans to return to WWE.

articles.title: Supplements: what do athletes take and why?
articles.summary: There is a long list of supplements taken by elite athletes in the pursuit of marginal gains - what do they take and why?
articles.body:
It was at the 1992 Olympics in Barcelona when the mutterings about a new "secret weapon" started.

Dozens of Great Britain athletes had been taking a new product that increased muscle mass and improved athletic performance – a "wonder pill" that didn't fall foul of any doping rules.

Now found in tubs and bags on many supermarket shelves and tagged in your social feeds, it is the supplement of choice for millions of people and one of the most scientifically researched.

But back then, when it came on the scene at the very top of British elite sport, there were suspicions and stigma around the use of any substance described as 'performance enhancing' – even if it was legal.

From the minute an athlete wakes, to the moment they go to bed, they are thinking about how they can optimise their performance and recovery.

Today, creatine is just one of a long list of supplements taken by elite athletes in this pursuit of marginal gains. Some help with muscle size and strength, while others correct deficiencies in the diet.

"There are various reports in the literature of some studies that say maybe up to 90% of athletes take supplements. I often jokingly say that means 10% are lying," says Prof Graeme Close, professor of human physiology at Liverpool John Moores University.

"The sports teams that I've worked in, I think that's probably closer to 100% of athletes will be taking some form of supplementation."

So, what do supplements actually do and why do athletes take them? And in the world of strict liability, where elite athletes are solely responsible for what they put in their bodies, how do they make sure they stay clean?

While experts like Close advocate for seeking to meet nutritional needs through food in the first instance, it may not always be possible or practical to do this - and that is where supplements come in.

Take, for example, creatine, which is found naturally in meat and fish.

"You would need the best part of a kilogram of raw chicken a day to get the amount of creatine you need," says Close. But it is unsafe to eat raw poultry because of the food poisoning risk from harmful bacteria.

Creatine is a natural compound in the body produced in the kidneys, liver and pancreas. It is a quick source of energy for muscles, which is especially important for short-duration, high intensity activities such as sprinting.

Its big break as a supplement came in the 1990s when two scientists who had been researching it for two decades shared their findings with Steve Jennings, whose Maxim sports nutrition company supplied products to the British Olympic team.

During the 1992 Barcelona Games, investigative reporter Doug Gillon had learned of a 'secret trial' involving British athletes and seen a box of their Ergomax C150 – effervescent creatine tablets. He wrote that if the scientists' claims - that creatine could improve explosive athletic performance by 1-3% - were true, then "sport may never be the same again".

In terms of sport supplements and nutrition, he was right. By the time of the next Olympics in 1996, an estimated 80% of athletes were taking creatine, and since then it has become mainstream, with research suggesting there may be cognitive benefits as well as physical.

According to the Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition, the creatine breakthrough of the 1990s had "launched a new era in sports nutrition" and "sparked exploration into other supplements".

The global dietary supplements market size was valued at $209.5bn (£154bn) in 2025 and is projected to grow to $431.7bn (£317.4bn) by 2033, according to Grand View Research. , external

Close, who oversaw nutrition for last year's British and Irish Lions rugby union tour, sees supplements as the "final piece of the jigsaw" rather than a starting point.

"What we're talking about is small margins of benefit, where actually these athletes who focus on the food, I think what you often find is that they've got the big-ticket items right," he says.

"So they're seeing great performance benefits because their overall diet is immaculate.

"They might be missing out on the one per-centers, but they've really nailed the 99 per-centers. And they often do better than those who chase the one per-centers but have not given enough attention to the 99 per-centers."

Australian cyclist Nicole Frain agrees, adding: "I'm a pretty big believer that they are called sport supplements. They are there to supplement the things you already do right.

"I don't think supplements are the answer to fix my problems.

"You need to be eating a balanced diet, training well, sleeping right, recovering well, hydrating – all of those things – before we add in all of the extras."

Close puts protein powders top of the list of supplements taken by athletes he works with, followed by creatine and vitamin D.

Protein powders maximise muscle repair and contribute to muscle growth, while creatine is a quick source of energy for muscles and important in short-duration, high-intensity activities like sprinting. Vitamin D, meanwhile, is essential for bone health and supports muscle function.

Other popular supplements include carbohydrate gels, which Close says were key in the first sub-two hour marathon run earlier this year by Kenyan long-distance runner Sabastian Sawe.

"As sport nutritionists we were all fascinated at what the fuelling programme was, and it was the sports drinks and gels that played a huge part of that fuelling," Close says.

"There was a calculation done of what it would take to break the two-hour marathon, and that did involve making sure that over 100 grams of supplemental carbohydrate were ingested per hour.

"And the reports coming out of the recent sub-two-hour marathon was that it was 110 grams of carbohydrate per hour that was achieved."

Supplements can improve performance, but there is an uneasy ring to describing them as 'performance enhancing' because of the association with banned substances and anti-doping rule violations.

So what determines whether something is on the World Anti-Doping Agency's (Wada) banned list?

"For Wada to put anything on the list, it's got to hit two out of three criteria: dangerous to health, performance enhancing, and against the spirit of sport," Close explains.

"So just because something enhances performance, if it's not dangerous to health and not against the spirit of sport, Wada will not touch it.

"Though something like an anabolic steroid, where it's against the spirit of sport to be injecting yourself for a performance benefit, it's dangerous to health and it's performance enhancing - that hits all three."

But taking a supplement still carries anti-doping risks.

"No guarantee can be given that any particular supplement is free from prohibited substances," UK Anti-Doping advice states, urging athletes to "be vigilant" in using them.

And if you test positive for a prohibited substance, consuming it unintentionally can result in the same four-year ban as if you deliberately took it.

There are supplement-testing programmes which batch test products before they are sold to make sure they do not contain any Wada-prohibited substances.

One of those is Informed Sport, which says as many as one in 10 supplements is contaminated with ingredients and compounds prohibited in sport and points to a study carried out by the Anti-Doping Knowledge Centre that showed product contamination was responsible for 8% of all anti-doping violations between 2005 and 2022.

While Informed Sport is a very well used system among athletes, Wada makes it clear that quality assurance schemes can reduce but do not eliminate the risk of an anti-doping infringement.

If you do accept the risk, you need to be organised to keep track.

In the case of Great Britain rower Heidi Long, it takes a spreadsheet.

"I've recorded the batch number of every product that I've taken and its expiry date because if you take it after the expiry date the Informed Sport [certification] is no longer viable," she says.

Close says he has also done site visits to factories to see where the supplements are made to check the manufacturing processes because "the risk of failing a drugs test is huge".

There are risks to the general population too, he adds, saying: "You can be buying supplements off the internet that are made in somebody's garage and you've got no idea of the manufacturing processes."

He points to studies on creatine products which have found there is no creatine in them and so "you're completely wasting your money" and that in the worst case scenario it may contain substances that are dangerous to your health.

"So it is really important that the message is that while they can play a small role, the safety considerations are the key factor," he says.

There is, however, more than one way for an elite athlete to chase a competitive edge – and some are going back to basics.

For every trending supplement, there is an unprocessed, wholefood alternative – from the anti-inflammatory benefits of turmeric, staving off cramp with pickle juice or consumption of high-nitrate foods like beetroot before competition.

It is what Close calls a "food-first" or "food-only" approach and something he says every athlete should use as a starting point.

The latest to have its moment in the spotlight is an ancient Ethiopian grain called teff.

Used for thousands of years in traditional east African diets, teff is now making its mark globally in performance nutrition.

In comparison to other popular grains like wheat, rice and quinoa, teff has a high mineral content and is rich in calcium, iron and vitamin C. Naturally gluten-free and good for the gut, it is also unique for being a 'complete' protein, meaning it provides all nine essential amino acids required for human nutrition.

These superfood credentials have caught the attention of some of the world's best athletes over the years, from Olympic champion marathon runner Haile Gebrselassie to seven-time Grand Slam singles champion Venus Williams, and it is now becoming a more common sight on UK supermarket shelves.

British boxer Fran Hennessy was introduced to teff by her nutritionist and it is now part of her daily routine.

"I've never looked back," she says. "What I'm putting in my body is good fuel and energy and teff has so much. It energises you so much before a workout and it gives you the fibre you need."

As well as boosting her performances, Hennessy credits teff with being key to recovery.

She says: "Each meal I'm having there's a reason behind and everything that's in it there's a reason behind... I know what I'm putting in my body is fuelling me, recovering me, energising me."

Cost is another consideration when athletes are deciding on supplements.

"The supplement industry is really expensive," says Long. "And we're definitely not made of money. So I think it's really picking and choosing when you want to put that investment in."

She says it makes sense to have more supplements around racing time "when the performance is super critical and very time dependent".

"[But] on a daily basis if I can get the protein intake from my dinner and a glass of milk or yoghurt and breakfast then actually I was going to be eating that food anyway so it's not as expensive."

"I would much rather enjoy a coffee in the morning with friends or while I'm working rather than have one of the gels," she says. "Some of the gels ... you'll end up holding your nose when you take it.

"I guess it's just like the enjoyment of what you're taking, you know, it's nicer to eat food than it is to take supplements."

articles.title: Los datos más sorprendentes de Premier Padel: una promesa como el jugador con más ganadores
articles.standfirst: Aimar Goñi se cuela como uno de los grandes protagonistas de la primera mitad de año
articles.summary: Aimar Goñi se cuela como uno de los grandes protagonistas de la primera mitad de año
articles.body: El frenetismo de Premier Padel, con decenas de pruebas cada temporada, hace que muchas veces no quede tiempo para analizar lo que ocurre tras cada torneo. Sin embargo, las semanas de descanso que atraviesa el circuito profesional sirven como punto de inflexión para sacar a la luz algunas de las estadísticas más relevantes de lo que va de curso, con varias sorpresas en las categorías más cotizadas. El portal ‘Padel Intelligence’, referente en el análisis de datos, ha publicado el balance de su base de datos de la primera parte del año. Entre las métricas más destacadas figura la del jugador con más winners por partido en lo que va de 2026, un privilegio que se ha llevado una de las grandes revelaciones del circuito: Aimar Goñi. El navarro ha brillado con su pegada y envergadura, liderando la tabla con 30,3 golpes ganadores por encuentro. Le siguen, a bastante distancia, Ale Galán con 24,4 y Javi Garrido con 23,3. Aimar empezó la campaña junto a Enri Goenaga, pero ha sido al lado de Edu Alonso con quien ha logrado explotar en los últimos meses. Su compañero es un drive clásico, sin tanto poderío aéreo, lo que permite al joven revés asumir galones y maximizar sus cualidades ofensivas. Esos espectaculares 30,3 winners nacen principalmente de su smash, faceta donde también lidera el circuito con 13,6 remates ganadores por partido. En esta estadística le sigue de nuevo Galán (11,9), mientras que Javi Leal cierra el podio con 11,4. Sin embargo, el recurso de Goñi no se limita al remate. El navarro también ocupa el primer puesto en ganadores de volea, con 8,75 por choque, situándose por encima de Arturo Coello (7,10) y de Ale Galán (7,02), a quien el consenso general señala como el mejor voleador del planeta. El volumen de winners exige asumir riesgos, y las cifras de Aimar se entienden mejor al observar sus errores no forzados. Jon Sanz es el jugador que más fallos ha acumulado en estos meses, con 16,35 por encuentro. Justo por detrás aparece el propio Goñi, con 15,21 errores no forzados por partido. Es ahí donde reside el gran margen de mejora del revés navarro: si logra sostener su producción ofensiva reduciendo el número de concesiones, se consolidará entre los mejores del planeta. El espejo donde mirarse en términos de consistencia es Coki Nieto, quien lidera la clasificación de los jugadores más fiables. El madrileño comete apenas 5,8 errores no forzados por duelo. Le siguen Martín Di Nenno con 6,8 y Lucas Bergamini con 6,9. En el pádel de élite, la fiabilidad para forzar el fallo ajeno resulta tan determinante como la capacidad para definir. Estas métricas ofrecen además un reflejo fiel de las dinámicas de pareja. Jon Sanz, el jugador que más falla, asume mayores riesgos al estar respaldado por la solidez de Nieto, el que menos concede. Por su parte, Bergamini sostiene el esquema de una dupla cuyo compañero figura entre los principales rematadores. En esa lista de pegadores ya no aparece Leo Augsburger, líder el año pasado, ya que la presencia de Juan Lebrón a su lado equilibra el reparto de tareas ofensivas. Ocurre lo contrario con Goñi o Galán, acompañados por perfiles de contención que exigen un mayor volumen de resolución por su parte. El caso más ilustrativo es el de los número uno. Ni Arturo Coello ni Agustín Tapia encabezan de forma aislada estas clasificaciones individuales, pero su equilibrio entre un volumen altísimo de definición repartido entre ambos y una tasa de error reducida —sin llegar a los mínimos de Nieto o Di Nenno debido a su estilo agresivo— los consolida en lo más alto del ranking de Premier Padel.

articles.title: Mikey Lewis: Hull KR playmaker banned for two matches for dangerous contact with Warrington Wolves' Ewan Irwin
articles.summary: Mikey Lewis has received a two-match ban for dangerous contact which will see him miss Rounds 25 and 26 of Super League; he had just returned from a four-match ban for a headbutt; round 24 of Super League commences from Thursday August 20, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Lewis was sent to the sin bin when his studs hit Irwin's ankle as he sent up a kick, and he has been given a Grade C charge.

The ban will take effect from Round 25 which means he can play against Toulouse on Saturday but then will miss games against Wigan Warriors and Huddersfield Giants.

That would mean he returns for the final round of the regular season.

It is not known yet if the Robins will appeal the ban.

Lewis had just returned from a four-match ban which he copped for a headbutt the last time Hull KR played Warrington.

During that period, his side won all four matches without their star half-back.

It was wondered whether Hull KR would stick with Ryan Hampshire due to their winning run, but Peters opted to bring Lewis back in, citing the learning curve he has been on over the last month.

However, Peters faces a conundrum that Lewis is available for just two of their four remaining matches until the play-offs.

At the time, Warrington Wolves head coach Sam Burgess referred to the contact as "very dangerous" while Peters said he did not feel there was any "intent" behind the action.

Hull KR's Tevita Pangai Jr has also received a four-match ban, which means he would not be available until the semi-finals, if Peters' side were to make it that far.

He was cited for 'late contact on a passer' in three instances, two charged as Grade A and one as Grade B.

Due to already having a hefty amount of points on his record due to an eye gouge on Leeds Rhinos' Jake Connor earlier in the season, he could potentially not play in a Rovers shirt again.

Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live. The remaining five matches will be broadcast on Sky Sports+ .

articles.title: Backstage WWE and AEW Rumors on Roman Reigns, Ruby Soho and More
articles.summary: Roman Reigns continues to draw some of the biggest reactions of any WWE Superstar on the roster, but how is he viewed from a character standpoint behind the scenes?
articles.body:
Roman Reigns continues to draw some of the biggest reactions of any WWE Superstar on the roster, but how is he viewed from a character standpoint behind the scenes?

The answer to that question headlines this collection of pro wrestling rumors, featuring reports from the most trusted insiders, also including the in-ring status of Ruby Soho and more.

World heavyweight champion Roman Reigns receives deafening reactions when he enters the arena on Monday nights, but that is not always reflective of the character that appears on WWE Raw.

The Tribal Chief is an egotistical narcissist who has managed to again insulate himself with The Bloodline, forming a shield around himself with his family—the same family he has openly gaslit to get what he wants from them.

False Finish reported that Reigns is listed as a heel by WWE Creative internally.

That is in line with the manner in which he has been booked of late. The way he talked down to, berated and belittled Solo Sikoa on the most recent episode of Raw before getting his comeuppance certainly felt like the actions of a villain.

Hopefully, the idea that Reigns is a heel in the eyes of WWE officials will only help improve this third chapter of the Bloodline, which has struggled to make the same impact as the original incarnation, which can be attributed to creative inconsistencies and too much ambiguity.

Ruby Soho has not wrestled a match for All Elite Wrestling since February 7, 2024, when she teamed with Saraya in a losing effort against Kris Statlander and Willow Nightingale during a taping of Rampage.

Since then, she has given birth to a child and opened a cafe called Victory Road with her partner, Angelo Parker. Amid all of the major life changes, there has been little update on her AEW status or a potential return to the squared circle...until now.

Sean Ross Sapp of Fightful Select reported: "Fightful Select sources are told that Ruby Soho was actually at the AEW tapings in Cincinnati way back in June. We were also told that Ruby was getting clearances from AEW medical for her eventual return to the ring."

He added: "We did hear that some ideas had been floated around for Ruby over the past number of months, but have not learned of anything solid being enacted. Ruby has not been a regular backstage at AEW, either."

While there is no clear indication she will be back any time soon, Sapp's report should be considered a "win" for Soho's fans, who have not heard much from or about the star of late.

If she does return to the squared circle, she will return to an AEW women's division that is much different from the one she last encountered over two years ago.

False Finish also reported WWE Hall of Famer Rey Mysterio pushed for El Fiscal's inclusion in the tournament to crown a No. 1 contender to Roman Reigns' World Heavyweight Championship.

El Fiscal squared off against Rey Fenix Monday night on Raw. Ultimately, he lost to the AAA cruiserweight champion, but he delivered a solid performance that may result in more exposure in the coming weeks and months.

Mysterio is a tremendous ambassador for lucha libre and the talent in AAA. He is a general manager on the screen, but if there is anyone who can influence the power players backstage and get more TV exposure for the young stars tearing it up in Mexico, it is The Master of the 619.

El Fiscal, 26, is the son of legendary luchador Abismo Negro.

articles.title: 6 NHL Free-Agent Landing Spots for Vladimir Tarasenko Amid Rumors
articles.summary: With NHL training camp approaching, there are a few big-name players still looking for a place to play and Vladimir Tarasenko might be the most accomplished among them.
articles.body:
With NHL training camp approaching, there are a few big-name players still looking for a place to play and Vladimir Tarasenko might be the most accomplished among them.

The 34-year-old sniper had a bounce-back season with Minnesota last year after a disappointing campaign in Detroit the previous year. In 75 games, he had 23 goals and 24 assists for 47 points.

He had five goals and eight assists on the power play, and if there's a good way to market him to a team in need, it's his ability to help on the man advantage.

Surely there's a market for a player who can still produce offensively and brings Stanley Cup-winning experience? If his defensive effort were stronger, we might not be writing about him.

That said, anyone who can chip in close to 50 points in a season should have a market and we've picked out some teams who could definitely make use of Tarasenko's skills.

When it came to scoring last season, the Flames were not associated with that in any way. Calgary scored the fewest goals in the NHL (208) and had the league's second-worst power play (16.2 percent).

With that lack of offensive output, how could the Flames not be interested in Vladimir Tarasenko?

He would have been Calgary's leading scorer with his output last season. He scored more goals (23) than any other Flames player. Even though his season was solid, it wasn't the best of his career, yet it was still better than anyone else on the Calgary roster.

The case for adding Tarasenko is easy because he would help the Flames score more goals and potentially win more games. His defensive play might not always be up to snuff, but it was an offensive desert in Calgary last season.

And if Tarasenko plays well and the Flames aren't in the playoff race, it would be an opportunity for Calgary to move him to a contender.

Chicago had a bold offseason, bringing back Patrick Kane and adding Bowen Byram to the defense. With how poor their offense was last season, those two will help give them a lift.

But with so many young players figuring out their games in the NHL, adding Vladimir Tarasenko to the mix could give the Blackhawks a bit of insurance in case they can't.

Chicago is well-acquainted with Tarasenko after his many seasons with the St. Louis Blues and again last season in Minnesota. It knows about his shot, how he works on the power play and how he would fit into its lineup.

Although you could argue that bringing Kane back fills that need, you could also suggest Chicago just needs more, especially with Connor Bedard likely missing the start of the season.

Tarasenko and his goal-scoring could give the Blackhawks a boost when times get tough for their younger players.

This offseason has been fascinating for Edmonton following the arrival of new head coach Mike Babcock, but they're also a team looking to get back to the Stanley Cup Final.

They're not hurting for offense with Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl, but bringing in an experienced shooter like Vladimir Tarasenko could give them the cover they need for younger players.

While the Oilers are a team that may not need more firepower, they are looking at potentially throwing rookie Isaac Howard back into the fire again this season.

Although the 22-year-old struggled in the NHL last year, he had a solid AHL season. But with a new coach and the same high expectations, supporting him with a veteran like Tarasenko could be the kind of depth Edmonton is looking for.

Adding Tarasenko to an already outstanding Oilers power play would be a case of the rich getting richer, but more scoring depth for Edmonton at 5-on-5 would be a good thing.

The Flyers' boldness this summer in trying to land Leo Carlsson puts them firmly on any list for available scoring talent, and Vladimir Tarasenko more than fits that bill.

His scoring skill and great work on the power play would give Philly at least one ace in the hole and it would also give fellow Russian, Matvei Michkov, someone to learn from.

The Flyers had the NHL's worst power play last season (15.7 percent) and while they want their current players to get better at it, adding a shooter and playmaker like Tarasenko could give their man advantage some needed juice.

If there's a catch with adding Tarasenko, how coach Rick Tocchet would handle the player's more offense-minded style of play would be worth keeping an eye on.

Part of Toronto's offseason makeover under new GM John Chayka involved basically rebuilding the entire third and fourth lines.

While that's good for toughening up the defense, it may leave the Maple Leafs' offense relying too heavily on their star players to do all the scoring.

Adding Vladimir Tarasenko as an option on the cheap could give them the scoring depth to help buoy them.

His talent offensively is still strong, as he demonstrated last season in Minnesota.

The Leafs have Auston Matthews, William Nylander and John Tavares to lead the offense and adding Gavin McKenna in the draft should help them score more, but you can't help but look at the Toronto roster and think it needs more.

Tarasenko has some limitations defensively, but new coach Jim Hiller's system should help to that end.

The Canucks were the NHL's worst team last season for many reasons, but a big one was that they just didn't score enough goals.

That issue doesn't seem set to resolve itself heading into the new year, as they're lacking depth in a big way, which should put Vladimir Tarasenko on their radar.

His 23 goals would have tied him for the team lead with Jake DeBrusk, and his 47 points would have been the fourth-most on the squad. Although he wouldn't solve Vancouver's problems, he would help address them by adding another guy who can contribute to the offense.

If there's a catch here, it's that Tarasenko might not want to join a team that is unlikely to be a playoff contender, never mind a Stanley Cup hopeful. However, this could be a situation where he can play himself into a contender by the deadline if he shows out. It may not be the most ideal way to go about it, but it's an option.

articles.title: Revolución en Hyundai: su superventas Tucson cambia tanto que no lo reconocerás
articles.standfirst: La quinta generación del superventas coreano estrena un diseño mucho más contundente, gana espacio y recupera algo que muchos conductores echaban de menos: los botones físicos
articles.summary: La quinta generación del superventas coreano estrena un diseño mucho más contundente, gana espacio y recupera algo que muchos conductores echaban de menos: los botones físicos
articles.body: El Tucson es la joya de la corona de Hyundai: el modelo más vendido de la marca coreana en Europa en el último lustro de forma constante... y el SUV compacto preferido por el público del continente. Por eso ha puesto toda la carne en el asador para su renovación. Salta a la vista que es una renovación/revolución en lo estético la que Hyundai ha aplicado para la quinta generación, que se presentará mundialmente en el próximo Salón del Automóvil de París (a mediados de octubre). El nuevo Tucson no se parecerá a otros modelos de la marca coreana... siguiendo una estrategia de diseño muy particular, en la que casi cada modelo tiene identidad propia. Sí que vemos rasgos familiares en el concepto de iluminación frontal, con una tira horizontal que cruza todo el morro como ya sucede en el Kona, pero reinterpretado. Pero el resto de sus líneas son más dramáticas, lejos de la redondez del modelo actual.  Es un Tucson más cuadrado y rectilineo, adoptando un estilo más parecido a sus primos de Kia y a su hermano mayor, el Santa Fe, pero con una personalidad distinta.  En cuanto a dimensiones, el nuevo Tucson crece seis centímetros hasta los 4,7 metros y también es más ancho (+4 cm) y con más distancia entre ejes (+3 cm). Con estas cifras cabe esperar una mejor habitabilidad interior, aparte de una presencia más contundente sobre la carretera. Eso sí, su nueva talla es más de SUV grande que de compacto, por lo que quizá sus rivales cambien y el Tucson 2027 mire hacia modelos como el Toyota RAV4, el Skoda Kodiaq El interior también da un vuelco total... donde lo más destacado no es el nuevo concepto de cuadro de relojes (minimalista) o la gran pantalla central. Lo que más destaca es la vuelta de los botones físicos Sobre las mecánicas, de momento sólo se ha confirmado que habrá versiones híbridas y enchufables, aunque es probable que se mantengan versiones térmicas como complemento. Más difícil será ver un Tucson eléctrico, algo que de momento Hyundai reserva para su gama Ioniq. En las fotos que Hyundai ha ofrecido para el lanzamiento también aparece una versión XRT con una estética off road aún más extrema, algo que ya había mostrado en el Santa Fe.

articles.title: WWE's Growing Problem with Oba Femi
articles.summary: Oba Femi has had a breakout year for WWE, enjoying a magical run through the main roster that has seen him dominate the competition, defeat Brock Lesnar in two of their three wars and win the King of the Ring tournament.
articles.body:
Oba Femi has had a breakout year for WWE, enjoying a magical run through the main roster that has seen him dominate the competition, defeat Brock Lesnar in two of their three wars and win the King of the Ring tournament.

Femi is incredibly popular with fans and looks every bit the future star that Lesnar labeled him at the conclusion of their Hell in a Cell Match at SummerSlam.

However, The Ruler's meteoric rise and early career triumphs are not without a significant growing problem for WWE.

Femi exploded onto the scene in WWE and within three months of his main roster call-up, defeated Lesnar clean and in the center of the ring.

He lost the next matchup, but put an end to The Beast Incarnate's Hall of Fame-worthy career inside the unforgiving confines of Hell in a Cell at SummerSlam in their third encounter.

There is no better way for WWE to have introduced Femi to the fans and announced him as the next big thing than the way he has been booked.

However, when a star arrives in WWE and immediately conquers the seemingly unconquerable, there are only so many directions they can go and still maintain their momentum.

For Femi, beating and retiring Lesnar was a blessing and a curse in that the only logical next step for him is vanquishing Roman Reigns or CM Punk and claiming one of the company's top two titles.

WWE, however, appears content to deliver the slow build, with Femi likely winning the men's Royal Rumble match in January 2027 and challenging for one of those titles at WrestleMania 43.

The Show of Shows is still nearly nine months away.

The only thing that can possibly happen between now and then is that Femi loses momentum. Even his rivalry with Bron Breakker, a showdown between two men expected to carry WWE well into the future, feels like a step down for The Ruler.

That is not an indictment of Breakker. There are levels to this, though, and to suggest he has not been adversely affected by baffling creative would be an understatement.

A match with Femi clearly means more to Breakker than it does to The Ruler.

That there is unlikely to be a clean finish means the two will keep each other busy for a few months. That will benefit one half of the pairing while leaving fans to speculate when Femi will step up to Reigns.

WWE Creative has not had the best track record over the last two years, with head-scratching decisions hurting story progression, leading to nonsensical developments and stunting the growth of some of its top young stars.

Case in point, Breakker, who returned at WrestleMania 42, defeated Seth Rollins at Backlash, but ultimately lost that feud and has been saddled in a tag team with Austin Theory ever since.

It would be fair to question whether WWE can effectively push Femi in a way that does not undo everything it has accomplished with him to this point.

One loss here, or a bad segment of TV there, could do considerable damage and threaten it all. Lesnar put Femi in a prime position to go out and succeed as the new smashing badass in WWE.

If someone in the room overthinks a single match or moment, it could unravel, and Femi's aura and popularity will be adversely affected. Again, nine months is a long time, with plenty of opportunities for someone to make a call that sabotages the biggest slam dunk the company has had in decades.

Yes, WWE has carefully booked Femi to this point, except for the guaranteed title shot he willingly gave up to battle Lesnar at SummerSlam. But that was a momentary lapse with little ill-effect.

The company will not be that lucky if it fails him on the road to what feels like an inevitable and appropriate coronation as soon as WrestleMania next spring.

Holding off on crowning Femi champion at that event would only deepen WWE's growing problem.

articles.title: NHL Announces Global Games Featuring Bruins, Oilers in Munich and Cologne for 2027 Schedule
articles.summary: The NHL is going to Germany for four regular-season games on the 2027-28 schedule.
articles.body:
The NHL is going to Germany for four regular-season games on the 2027-28 schedule.

According to a release from the NHL, Munich and Cologne will host games as part of the Global Games series. The Boston Bruins will play two games at the SAP Garden, and Lanxess Arena will host two games featuring the Edmonton Oilers.

Dates and opponents for the games will be announced at some point after the 2026-27 NHL season begins.

Germany first hosted an NHL regular season game in October 2011 when the Buffalo Sabres and Los Angeles Kings played at O2 World in Berlin.

Thursday's announcement comes in the wake of FC Bayern, the Munich-based Bundesliga soccer club, entering into a multiyear partnership with the NHL to help support the growth of the NHL in Germany and Bayern in the North America.

Germany is scheduled to host regular season NHL contests in at least each of the next three seasons. The 2026-27 campaign will feature the Ottawa Senators and Chicago Blackhawks playing two games in Düsseldorf at PSD Bank Dome on Dec. 18 and 20.

The games will provide a homecoming for JJ Peterka and Leon Draisaitl. Peterka, who was traded to the Bruins in June, is from Munich. The 24-year-old put up 47 points in 82 games for the Buffalo Sabres last season.

Draisaitl, who was born in Cologne, led Germany to the quarterfinals at the 2026 Olympics in his first-ever appearance at the Winter Games.

The 2026-27 regular season is expanding to 84 games for the first time since 1993-94. The season begins on Sept. 29 with the reigning Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes raising their banner against the Florida Panthers.

articles.title: Max Verstappen, Red Bull F1 Agree to 4-Year Contract Extension amid Mercedes Rumors
articles.summary: Red Bull Racing announced Thursday that Max Verstappen has signed an extension through the 2030 Formula One season.
articles.body:
Red Bull Racing announced Thursday that Max Verstappen has signed an extension through the 2030 Formula One season.

"I am really pleased with the contract extension," the four-time F1 champion said . "We have the best people and I'm excited to keep working together with everyone to get back to the top again. This remains the ultimate goal that all of us have been working towards and will continue to pursue. I want to thank Red Bull, (team principal Laurent Mekies) and everyone at Oracle Red Bull Racing for the trust they put in me."

York Responded to Ad on Prostitution Site Before Arrest

Verstappen was runner-up to Lando Norris in the 2025 drivers' standings. He had a sluggish start to the year and mounted a comeback attempt in the second half.

Back in March, the 28-year-old suggested he could walk away from Formula One altogether at the end of the current season.

Verstappen's performance on the track added some more uncertainty , with Mercedes having been linked with a blockbuster move in the past. More recently, McLaren emerged as a possible option .

Alas, Verstappen continues to believe in Red Bull's direction, and this is a significant show of faith in Mekies, who replaced Christian Horner as team principal last July.

Verstappen sits sixth in the standings and has yet to notch a victory. At the very least, any title challenge is likely out of the question, and remaining in sixth would be his worst finish since 2017.

The Dutchman's new contract ties him to Red Bull for the remainder of the decade. In theory, that should provide further doubt as to his status for the foreseeable future.

Should Verstappen's malaise extend into 2027 and beyond, the same concerns could once again emerge.

articles.title: Robot Crashes Into Electrical Box in Viral Video Ahead of World Humanoid Robot Games
articles.summary: Before Chinese robot firm Unitree can make good on its claim that a machine can outrun Usain Bolt, it needs to work on getting the bot to stop after crossing a finish line.
articles.body:
Before Chinese robot firm Unitree can make good on its claim that a machine can outrun Usain Bolt, it needs to work on getting the bot to stop after crossing a finish line.

Ahead of the second annual World Humanoid Robot Games, one of the machines was apparently so into its run that it made like Forrest Gump on a kickoff return by running directly into an electrical box before collapsing.

York Responded to Ad on Prostitution Site Before Arrest

Another video showed one of the robots running before crashing into a wall, leading to sparks flying from its chest.

According to Ben Cost of the New York Post , Unitree unveiled the robot it has dubbed "Superman" earlier this week. The company claims the bot has only been in development for three months, but its programming allows it to reach two meters (6.56 feet) from a standing high jump position and 12.66 meters per second while running.

The company claims those metrics surpass the standing high jump and running speed records "of all humans around the world."

Cost did note the speed of 12.66 meters per season would surpass Bolt's fastest-recorded speed of 12.2 m/s in 2009 when he set the world record in the 100 meters (9.58 seconds).

The bot's mishap came ahead of the World Humanoid Robot Games that will begin on Saturday in Beijing. There are 666 teams featuring 2,056 robots who will compete in various sporting events, including table tennis, kickboxing and a 4×100m relay.

articles.title: Ilja Dragunov's WWE Future Revealed in New Rumors After Former U.S. Champion's Contract Expired
articles.summary: Following an extended absence from WWE programming, former United States champion Ilja Dragunov is reportedly leaving the company.
articles.body:
Following an extended absence from WWE programming, former United States champion Ilja Dragunov is reportedly leaving the company.

According to PWInsider.com (h/t WrestlePurists ), Dragunov's departure comes amid the expiration of his WWE contract.

False Finish reported that WWE "would have liked Dragunov to stay with the company," but Dragunov made the decision to let his contract expire.

ESPN Addresses 'Completely False' Rumors About Future WWE Contract

After news of Dragunov exiting WWE broke, AEW international champion Kyle Fletcher acknowledged it by posting a photo from a match he had against Dragunov in 2019:

Born in Russia and raised in Germany, the 32-year-old Dragunov became a fixture in NXT UK after initially signing with WWE in 2019.

After a nearly yearlong reign as NXT United Kingdom champion, Dragunov made the move to NXT in 2022. He held the NXT Championship for over 200 days and had memorable rivalries with the likes of Trick Williams, Carmelo Hayes and Bron Breakker.

Dragunov got called up to WWE's main roster in 2024, but it wasn't long before he suffered a torn ACL, which kept him out of action for over a year.

On the Oct. 17 episode of SmackDown, Dragunov made his return to WWE programming as a surprise challenger for the United States Championship, and he beat Sami Zayn for the U.S. title on that night.

About two months later, Dragunov dropped the title to Hayes, and he struggled to secure consistent television time after that.

Dragunov lost a U.S. title rematch against Hayes in March, and then he made his final appearance on WWE programming about a month later when he competed in the Andre the Giant Memorial Battle Royal.

Many fans questioned where Dragunov had been for the past four months, and they now know that his WWE tenure has come to an end, making him a free agent who could be highly sought after on the open market.

As the second-biggest wrestling promotion in the world, AEW stands out as a potential landing spot for Dragunov.

AEW is staging its biggest pay-per-view of the year, All In, at Wembley Stadium in London on Aug. 30, and Dragunov stands out as a strong candidate to be a surprise entrant in the Casino Gauntlet match for a future AEW World Championship opportunity should he sign with the company.

New Japan Pro-Wrestling could also be a great fit for Dragunov's hard-hitting wrestling style, while TNA would potentially provide him with a chance to be a world title contender and main eventer immediately upon signing.

Regardless of where he ends up, Dragunov should have little issue landing on his feet and making a major impact in the pro wrestling world.

articles.title: El desgarrador testimonio de exfigura de Santa Fe tras perderlo todo por el juego: “Mi familia está destrozada”
articles.standfirst: Jonathan Gómez confesó sufrir de ludopatía: el duro momento que vive el exjugador de Santa Fe
articles.summary: Jonathan Gómez confesó sufrir de ludopatía: el duro momento que vive el exjugador de Santa Fe
articles.body: El fútbol suele vender historias de éxito, gloria deportiva y solvencia económica. Sin embargo, detrás del brillo de los estadios y las luces del triunfo se esconden realidades silenciosas pero devastadoras. Un claro ejemplo de esta paradoja es la reciente y desgarradora confesión del exfutbolista argentino Jonathan Gómez, recordado por la afición colombiana tras su paso por el Deportivo Pasto y su consagración como campeón con Independiente Santa Fe en el año 2016. En una desgarradora entrevista concedida al medio argentino Radiopolis, Gómez abrió su corazón para exponer la batalla interna que atraviesa por cuenta de su adicción a las apuestas: la ludopatía. Una confesión cruda que resuena en el ámbito internacional no solo como el testimonio de un exdeportista en ruinas, sino como una llamada de alerta sobre los riesgos del juego compulsivo en atletas de alto rendimiento. Jonathan Gómez, volante creativo de 36 años, construyó una carrera sobresaliente en el fútbol latinoamericano e internacional. Pasó por clubes de renombre en su país como Rosario Central, Banfield, Atlético Tucumán, San Martín de Tucumán y Racing Club de Avellaneda. Asimismo, expandió sus horizontes en Ligas de Brasil, España y Arabia Saudita. En Colombia, su fútbol creativo, dinámico y con llegada al gol dejó una huella imborrable. Vistió primero la camiseta del Deportivo Pasto y posteriormente se convirtió en figura indiscutible de Independiente Santa Fe, compartiendo la creación del juego con ídolos de la talla de Omar Pérez y levantando la novena estrella del cuadro 'cardenal' en la Liga local del año 2016, además de la Copa Suruga Bank en Japón. Sin embargo, a la par que construía su legado dentro de la cancha, un enemigo silencioso ganaba terreno en su vida cotidiana. "Perdí todo. Yo hoy perdí todo. Estoy en un proceso con mi familia en la cual está casi destrozada, tengo un proceso en el cual no sé si voy a poder volver a jugar al fútbol, que es lo que más me gusta", expresó el exfutbolista en su desgarrador relato. La ludopatía no solo devora el patrimonio financiero; destruye de manera sistemática los vínculos afectivos y la salud mental de quien la padece. Gómez detalló cómo el juego compulsivo transformó gradualmente su personalidad y su entorno social sin que él lo percibiera al principio: "Es algo que te distrae, no solamente en tu trabajo, sino en el día a día; te cambia el humor, te cambia tu personalidad. Hay momentos que ahora me siento a hablar con amigos que hoy estoy recuperando y me decían: 'Che, Jony, vos no estabas'. Y yo no me daba cuenta o me escondía. No quería ir o no hacía cosas. Lo mismo mi mujer: me decía 'Jony, ¿qué te pasa?'. Me irritaba todo el tiempo, porque el vicio te lleva a eso". El daño más severo para el mediocampista argentino radica en el ámbito familiar, donde el impacto emocional ha sido devastador tanto para su pareja como para sus hijos. "Perder a mi familia... Ahora cuando voy a ver a mis nenes y mis nenes lloran y me dicen: '¿Por qué papá se va?'. Eso fue lo más doloroso", confesó. El drama personal de Gómez traspasó las puertas de lo privado cuando meses atrás surgieron revelaciones sobre la magnitud financiera del problema. Según reportó el medio Doce TV, el jugador estuvo involucrado en un turbio episodio legal derivado de deudas adquiridas en plataformas de apuestas en línea. Tres meses antes de su confesión pública, Gómez denunció ante las autoridades haber sido presuntamente forzado a firmar cuatro pagarés en una escribanía por un monto de 505.000 dólares (una suma multimillonaria). Según sus declaraciones, esta abultada deuda se generó tras operar en plataformas clandestinas de casinos virtuales, exponiendo los peligros y las redes opacas que orbitan alrededor del juego ilegal.

articles.title: Brook makes Pakistan pay for dropped catch as England dominate first Test
articles.summary: England were 366-8 at stumps on a rain-marred second day, 195 runs ahead of Pakistan’s meagre first innings of 171.
articles.body:
Harry Brook has punished Pakistan for dropping him at the start of his innings with a quickfire 91 that strengthened England’s grip on the first cricket Test at Headingley.

England were 366-8 at stumps on a rain-marred second day on Thursday, 195 runs ahead of Pakistan’s meagre first innings of 171.

list 2 of 4 Pakistan beat West Indies to end 8 away Test losing streak and draw series

list 3 of 4 US cricket player Reddy receives eight-year ban for match-fixing

list 4 of 4 Cricket: India pace star Bumrah ruled out of tour of Sri Lanka

The only sadness for the crowd was that neither of their local Yorkshire heroes were able to post a century, with skipper Joe Root out for 66 before Brook fell late in the day.

Dan Lawrence, recalled after the international retirement of former captain Ben Stokes, made 51 and put on 120 with Brook in England’s first Test of the post-Bazball era.

Jordan Cox (73) and Root had earlier shared a third-wicket stand of exactly 150 before falling in quick succession to give Pakistan a glimmer of hope in the first of this three-Test series.

Brook, however, should then have been out for one when he edged Khurram Shahzad, only for diving Pakistan captain Salman Ali Agha, leading the side in place of the injured Babar Azam, to drop the chance at second slip.

Brook cashed in and was in sight of what would have been his first Test century at Headingley – and 11th in 39 matches overall – when he tried to turn left-arm spinner Ali Usman legside only for the ball to hit his leg before rattling the stumps.

The 27-year-old faced just 93 balls, hitting 13 fours.

It was the second time Brook, the number one batsman in the red-ball rankings, had been out in the 90s of a Test at Headingley following his 99 against India last year.

Usman was the pick of an otherwise largely ineffective all-pace attack with 5-92 in 23 overs, his maiden five-wicket haul in Test cricket coming in just his third match.

After dismissing three specialist batsmen, Usman removed tailenders Gus Atkinson and Ollie Robinson with successive deliveries before Jofra Archer survived the hat-trick ball.

England, following a washed-out morning session, resumed on 112-2 after pacemen Robinson (5-51) and Josh Tongue (5-46) had shared all 10 Pakistan wickets between them on Wednesday.

Root, at the start of his second stint as full-time England captain, was 37 not out with number three Cox – replacing the injured Jacob Bethell – unbeaten on 23.

Cox was severe on anything loose and the 25-year-old marked his second Test with a maiden fifty when he turned Mohammad Abbas past leg slip for his 10th boundary in 78 balls faced.

That was the end of the over, and just as Robinson and Tongue had reached their five-wicket hauls Wednesday off successive deliveries, the next ball saw Root follow Cox to fifty by whipping Mohammad Ali through the legside for four.

Cox was fortunate on 57 when Shahzad dropped a return catch off a miscued pull.

Usman succeeded where the seamers had failed, however, when a fending Cox edged a sharply turning delivery to wicket-keeper Mohammad Rizwan.

England’s 198-3 became 202-4 when Root was leg before wicket (LBW) four balls later to give the persevering Shahzad his lone wicket of an expensive 19 overs costing 111 runs.

The failure of Cox and Root to go on to a really big score arguably represented two more examples of the lack of ruthlessness that has plagued England during a run of seven defeats in their last nine Tests.

But it made little difference Thursday, with Pakistan’s plight summed up when Agha tried to run out the advancing Lawrence, after the ball rebounded off the batsman’s pads, only for his throw from slip to hit the back of Rizwan’s legs.

articles.title: Pipe Bueno rompe en llanto al revelar la adicción que casi destruye a su familia
articles.standfirst: La dura confesión de Pipe Bueno sobre sus adicciones y la crisis con Luisa Fernanda W: “Si no estaba borracho, estaba drogado"
articles.summary: La dura confesión de Pipe Bueno sobre sus adicciones y la crisis con Luisa Fernanda W: “Si no estaba borracho, estaba drogado"
articles.body: En una de las revelaciones más íntimas y vulnerables de su carrera, el cantante de música popular Pipe Bueno rompió el silencio sobre los oscuros momentos que atravesó debido al consumo descontrolado de alcohol y sustancias, una crisis marcada por la inseguridad y la mala gestión emocional que estuvo a punto de destruir su hogar con la creadora de contenido Luisa Fernanda W. Las declaraciones fueron hechas durante su participación en el pódcast 'Los hombres sí lloran', conducido por el actor Juan Pablo Raba. Allí, el intérprete colombiano se abrió para narrar cómo las presiones personales, los temores al mudarse de país (en su etapa de residencia en México) y la incapacidad de afrontar sus sentimientos lo llevaron a un laberinto del que le costó salir. El artista caleño explicó que durante mucho tiempo minimizó la importancia de la salud mental y desestimó la ayuda profesional. Sin embargo, al enfrentar incertidumbres laborales y personales, encontró en el licor y las sustancias un mecanismo de evasión. “Si estaba contento, bebía; si estaba aburrido, bebía... Llega uno a una montaña rusa entre licor y excesos. Me siento como nunca me había sentido en mi vida... estaba inseguro como nunca antes”, confesó el artista. El impacto emocional fue tal que Bueno llegó a admitir entre lágrimas: “Si no estaba borracho, estaba drogado. Se me empiezan a salir de control las emociones y para no gestionarlas, la manera era estar siempre en un estado alterado de conciencia”. La situación alcanzó su límite en México, contexto en el que la falta de estabilidad y los episodios de estrés provocaron que Luisa Fernanda W sufriera fuertes ataques de pánico. El momento definitivo ocurrió una mañana en la que Pipe Bueno despertó y descubrió que su pareja había tomado a sus dos hijos, Máximo y Domenic, para mudarse a un hotel. La decisión de separarse estaba prácticamente tomada en el corazón de la empresaria. Buscando una última oportunidad, el cantante fue tras ella, aceptando la gravedad del problema y pidiéndole que juzgara su futuro no por promesas, sino por sus acciones. A partir de ese instante, buscó acompañamiento profesional y terapéutico para iniciar un camino de rehabilitación que hoy lo mantiene sobrio desde hace varios meses. Tras la publicación de la entrevista, Luisa Fernanda W se pronunció a través de sus redes sociales para reflexionar sobre lo vivido a puerta cerrada. La generadora de contenido reconoció que mantener un hogar no siempre es perfecto y confesó la dureza del proceso: “Hubo momentos en los que me desenamoré. Decirlo así puede sonar fuerte, pero es real. También me volví a enamorar... porque hubo un momento en el que miré a los ojos a Pipe y le dije: 'No estás solo, te voy a apoyar'”. Luisa resaltó que, aunque para ella hubiera sido más sencillo alejarse dada su independencia económica y trayectoria, decidió quedarse por la fe en su familia, estableciendo límites claros y apoyándose en la espiritualidad mientras Pipe se hacía cargo de su propia recuperación. Hoy, recuperado y reencontrado con su música —proceso del cual nació su producción discográfica 'Aquí estoy yo'—, Pipe Bueno reflexiona sobre la importancia de pedir ayuda a tiempo y responsabilizarse de la salud mental. La pareja, que lleva casi ocho años junta, supera así una de sus pruebas más difíciles, enviando un mensaje sobre la sanación personal y la reconstrucción familiar a través del compromiso mutuo.
