articles.title: Jets' Woody Johnson Buys Stake in Aston Martin Aramco F1 Team
articles.summary: New York Jets owner Woody Johnson is entering a new business endeavor.
articles.body:
New York Jets owner Woody Johnson is entering a new business endeavor.

According to Jack Bell of NYJets.com, Johnson has acquired a stake in Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team. He will also join Aston Martin's board of directors as the vice chairman.

Johnson, the former US Ambassador to the United Kingdom, said his experience led to a "deep appreciation" for the car brand.

"During my time as US Ambassador to the United Kingdom, I have developed a deep appreciation for Aston Martin's rich history, as well as Lawrence Stroll's [the Aston owner] strategic vision and entrepreneurial spirit," Johnson said in the official Aston Martin announcement.

"I am excited to partner with him and contribute to the continued development of the team, with the ambition of building an organization capable of competing at the very highest level of the sport. We also share a commitment to growing the fanbase in the United States and introducing even more fans to the excitement of Formula 1."

According to ESPN's Rich Cimini , Johnson will handle the team's commercial growth, with a focus on the United States. He won't be involved in any day-to-day management duties.

Johnson has owned the Jets since 2000, when he purchased them for $635 million. He also purchased a 43 percent stake in Crystal Palace of the English Premier League in 2025 for $254 million, per Cimini.

Johnson said in a statement that he aims to partner with Stroll with "ambition of building an organization capable of competing at the very highest level of the sport" and wants to continue growing the sport of F1 in the United States.

Johnson and the Jets are well known across the pond, as the team holds international marketing rights for the United Kingdom and Ireland as part of the NFL's Global Markets Program. New York has played four regular-season games in London.

While Johnson will have an eye on his new Formula 1 team, he'll keep his focus on trying to get the Jets back to relevancy. The team is in a 15-year playoff drought and figures to be in for another tough year in 2026.

articles.title: Former Olympian Jenny Simpson Says She Has to End Running Career After Cardiac Arrest in Race
articles.summary: Olympic medalist Jenny Simpson says she will not run again after suffering cardiac arrest while running a pacer mile at a June track event in Raleigh.
articles.body:
Olympic medalist Jenny Simpson says she will not run again after suffering cardiac arrest while running a pacer mile at a June track event in Raleigh.

Simpson shared the update in a Thursday post on her Instagram .

After being treated for heart failure, Simpson said she was diagnosed with an inherited heart condition known as "Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy."

"Scar tissue within my heart disrupted its electrical system, triggering dangerous heart rhythms that ultimately caused my heart to stop," Simpson wrote.

Simpson continued, "My future is an incredible gift. It's hopeful, and it has great purpose. But my diagnosis also means it would be dangerous for me to return to running.

"That chapter has ended. Thankfully, my story hasn't."

Simpson, 36, represented the United States in three Olympics. She won 1,500-meter gold at the 2011 World Championships and bronze in the same event at the 2016 Rio Olympics.

The Associated Press first reported Simpson had been treated with CPR and an automated external defibrillator (AED) after collapsing on the track at the Sir Walter Miler on June 16.

Simpson wrote in her post that care "kept me alive until EMS arrived."

"After arriving at the hospital, I went into cardiac arrest again," Simpson wrote. "My heart continued to fail, and I was placed on life support before being transferred to Duke Hospital for more advanced heart failure support."

"And then, miraculously, my heart woke back up. My whole body proved remarkably resilient. Within days my heart and lungs were strong enough to work on their own."

Simpson went on to express gratitude for her running career, which spanned from winning four NCAA titles with Colorado to becoming the first American woman to medal in the Olympic 1,500-meter.

"I couldn't have written a better ending. To have my final run be a one mile race on the track, pacing young girls and running in community... I'm in awe of the goodness of what God has given me," Simpson wrote.

Simpson says she plans to remain Colorado while working on her recovery plan with doctors at Duke. She added she will discuss her recovery further in a CBS Saturday Morning appearance scheduled for this weekend.

Simpson initially retired from competitive running in 2024 after completing the New York City Marathon. She was named Fleet Feet's first Chief Running Officer, a job which includes designing training programs for the retailer, in February.

articles.title: Connor McDavid Talks NHL 27 99 Club, Macklin Celebrini, Oilers' 2026-27 Season, More in BR Interview
articles.summary: After many years of being widely viewed as the best hockey player in the world, Edmonton Oilers superstar center Connor McDavid is standing on his own in the upcoming EA Sports NHL 27 video game.
articles.body:
After many years of being widely viewed as the best hockey player in the world, Edmonton Oilers superstar center Connor McDavid is standing on his own in the upcoming EA Sports NHL 27 video game.

On Monday, EA named McDavid the inaugural member of the 99 Club in NHL 27, and the three-time Hart Memorial Trophy winner as NHL MVP spoke with Bleacher Report this week to discuss that and other topics.

A longtime fan of the EA Sports NHL video game franchise, McDavid noted how meaningful it is to be recognized as the flagship member of the 99 Club.

"I feel a little bit guilty in a sense because I made a joke about it a couple of years ago, so I feel like I maybe set this up for myself," McDavid said. "But it's a cool honor. It's a game that I played since I was a little kid. I know how big it is, what this game means to kids kind of growing up and loving the game. Every way possible, playing road hockey, pond hockey, playing real hockey and going home and playing video games with your siblings or your buddies, I know how much it means. I certainly know what it meant to me."

The 99 Club is something that originated in EA Sports' hugely popular Madden NFL video game franchise, and it has developed into one of the biggest honors in sports gaming.

McDavid expressed his belief that it can only be a good thing for hockey to have NHL 27 following in Madden's footsteps with the 99 Club, saying, "I think hockey is growing and it seems to be at a great rate. Any time we can be in the same breath as football, no matter the circumstances, it's a positive thing. I know what it means in the NFL, in Madden, to be part of the 99 Club. I hope that there will be many guys to join the NHL 99 Club. ... I hope it's something that grows over time and we can make it as big as Madden's 99 Club."

Madden may be the biggest sports video game franchise of all time, but the NHL video game franchise is sacred in its own right among hockey fans.

Fans of all ages have played and enjoyed the series since its inception, and McDavid himself is part of that group.

The six-time Art Ross Trophy winner as the NHL's leading point scorer fondly remembers some of the EA NHL battles he had with his brother while growing up, saying, "My household was pretty funny. I was a Leafs fan and my brother was a Senators fan, and we'd always play Leafs vs. Sens rivalry games. For me, though, I think my favorite memory is we always got it for Christmas. It almost became tradition for us to open the game and play later Christmas Day and get it rolling right then and there."

McDavid is 29 years old now and preparing to enter his 12th NHL season, but that hasn't stopped him from continuing to have fun with the EA Sports NHL video game series.

Peeling back the proverbial curtain a bit to offer a glimpse into what life is like for NHL players, McDavid divulged that playing the NHL video game is something they like to do together as a bonding activity.

"On the road, guys are bringing gaming systems with them wherever they're going," McDavid said. "I know in the playoffs we always set up kind of like a player lounge, and we've always got a PlayStation or Xbox going, and guys are playing each other head to head there. It's definitely something that bonds the guys even still. It doesn't matter how old you are, video games can still be fun, and certainly NHL is a great way to bond with each other."

While NHL teammates have the benefit of sitting down in the same room and playing the game together, that isn't the case for everyone.

In NHL 27, EA Sports is upping the ante with the addition of connected franchise for the first time ever. With connected franchise, up to 32 gamers can compete together in the same franchise mode.

McDavid views connected franchise as a great way to remain in contact with his longtime friends, saying, "For me, being away from home, finding a way to bond with my buddies back home and staying connected with my buddies back home has always been kind of a challenge. We've done it in many different ways, and sometimes gaming is a way for us to do that."

Another major inclusion in NHL 27 is unique, in-game presentations for all 32 NHL teams.

In an effort to make playing at every NHL arena feel as real as possible, NHL 27 features true-to-life pregame productions, and McDavid is looking forward to seeing the Oilers' atmosphere in virtual form.

"A little shoutout to our media team, they do a great job in Edmonton of getting the place going," McDavid said. "I know for me personally, skating out onto that ice, big playoff game, 'Enter Sandman' is playing, the crowd's going crazy, nothing is quite like it. I hope we can see that in the game. And the other thing for me is our anthem. The way the people scream 'O Canada' at the top of their lungs, it's such a special environment, it's such a fun place to play playoff hockey, and I hope it kind of translates to the game."

While McDavid is making history in NHL 27 with the 99 Club, San Jose Sharks sensation Macklin Celebrini received the honor of being the cover athlete for the game.

McDavid was on the cover of NHL 18, and he recalled what that was like to be part of that exclusive club.

"It's a tremendous honor," McDavid said. "I remember seeing my face on the cover of the game for the first time, and it really hits you. As fans we're always looking ahead to what's the next game and who's on the cover and what's the new features and all that. It's a proud moment to be on the cover, and something that I'm sure he's very proud of."

McDavid also had nothing but good things to say about Celebrini, who he has faced multiple times at the NHL level, while also joining forces with him as part of Team Canada at the 2026 Winter Olympics.

"He's special, there's no way around that," McDavid said of Celebrini. "Being his teammate, getting a chance to see him up close and personal, just how he works at such a young age and such a high-stress environment—obviously like the Olympics is—the kid just took it in stride. He's just himself, and I think that's an impressive thing. Obviously, playing against him, he's a tough matchup. There's no question he's one of the best players in the world, and you wanna shut him down when you can, and obviously produce as well on the other side. He's solid both ways."

McDavid and Celebrini figure to be among the biggest talking points when the 2026-27 NHL regular season officially starts on Sept. 29.

Opening night will feature five games, and one of them will see McDavid and the Oilers host the rival Vancouver Canucks.

McDavid confirmed that he is feeling the excitement for opening night even though he is more than a decade into his NHL career.

"There's always excitement opening night," McDavid said. "The first game of the season is always so highly anticipated and there's so much excitement. And then obviously opening night, to be a part of that is something we haven't had a chance to do in the last number of years, there's something to be said to play on that night. It means a lot, everybody's watching. I know I've been at home watching opening night and seeing the first look at the new season. It's an exciting night and something that we're excited to be a part of, and hoping to get off to a good start."

McDavid led the Oilers to back-to-back Stanley Cup Final appearances in 2024 and 2025 before the team suffered a first-round playoff exit last season.

Although McDavid acknowledged that a tough road is ahead for the Oilers and every other team because of how competitive the league is currently, he expressed confidence that the team will perform up to its lofty expectations.

"The parity has never been tighter," McDavid said. "Everybody can play, right from the best teams in the league right down to the teams that are vying for the first overall pick. It's tough every single night. The game is in an amazing place, but with that being said, it causes you to need to be ready to go each and every night because if you're not, I don't like your chances. We got our work cut out for us, we know that. We gotta build our program back to the standard that we think it needs to be at, and we'll do that. It'll start right away here."

With McDavid, Leon Draisaitl and Evan Bouchard leading the way, the Oilers have established themselves as perennial Stanley Cup contenders, and the expectations will likely be nothing less than that in 2026-27.

As such, the Oilers figure to be one of the most popular teams for gamers to utilize when NHL 27 is officially released for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S on Sept. 11.

articles.title: Meet teen superstar Yan Diomandé, the most expensive African soccer player in history
articles.summary: Yan Diomandé is set to have an incredibly bright future. At just 19, the attacker has signed for arguably the world’s biggest soccer team in Real Madrid and will begin his debut season for Los Blancos as they face Espanyol on Saturday.
articles.body: Yan Diomandé is set to have an incredibly bright future. At just 19, the attacker has signed for arguably the world’s biggest soccer team in Real Madrid and will begin his debut season for Los Blancos as they face Espanyol on Saturday. The Spanish giant signed the Ivory Coast international on a seven-year deal this summer, for a reported fee of $144.3 million. That not only makes him the most expensive African player in history, but one of the biggest transfers in all of soccer. But while many wax lyrical about his rags-to-riches story – one that saw him hone his skills in the United States – his is also a story of heartbreak and a reminder of the traps that lie in wait for young stars who aspire to become professionals. Diomandé was born in the city of Abidjan in the Ivory Coast. It was a humble childhood but one grounded by the importance of family and friends. A passion for soccer was there from the start and a young Diomandé could be found running on dirt pitches in just a pair of white sandals. In a letter he recently wrote for The Player’s Tribune, Diomandé says he was nicknamed after Brazilian legend Roberto Carlos because of his ability to strike the ball so hard. He was only getting started, but people could already see the natural ability that the youngster believed would one day take him to the top. He started playing more seriously for a local team where he saw his aspirations grow. It wasn’t long before he was telling friends he’d be the next Cristiano Ronaldo. The pivotal moment in that becoming a reality came when he was just 15. After representing his country at an under-17 tournament in Ghana, he caught the attention of scouts from around the world. All of a sudden, he was a boy in demand. But as is the case for a lot of young talent in the soccer industry, the teenager quickly became a commodity. Agents, coaches and teams all wanted to represent him, to sign him, to have some say in his future. Moving to Florida Eventually, through a convoluted arrangement of partnerships which stretched from Africa to the United States, Diomandé was offered the chance to join the DME Academy in Daytona Beach, Florida. He was just 15 at the time, but the move was supposed to help him develop in a professional environment which would prepare him for a life playing in the top echelons of the game. In truth, though, it was also a way of hiding him away from other agencies and teams that were sniffing around the player. The idea was that he would stay in the US until he was old enough to sign a professional contract at 18, per FIFA guidelines. So, with just a suitcase and a dream, Diomandé left his home and family in Africa on a one-way journey to the US. Picking him up from the airport in Miami was DME Academy’s director of soccer Todd Eason, a man who would become a father figure for a boy being pulled in every which direction. “Because he only spoke French, our communication was very limited on our drive back from Miami, which was four hours away,” the now Miami FC General Manager told CNN Sports over the phone. “We just exchanged little messages on Google Translate to try to get to know each other. But I also had other French-speaking players on the team, so it was kind of let me just hurry back to campus, let me introduce him to others that speak the language and try to get him comfortable there.” At DME, a small team of players would train up to six times a week and balance that with their studies. It allowed Diomandé to learn English and get used to a very different way of life. He quickly formed bonds within the team and, despite staying relatively quiet, would come alive on the pitch. He surprised even Eason, who had only watched his video highlights until then. Diomandé was not just faster than everyone else, he was more intelligent on the ball and was already confident leading by example. “I assumed we just had another strong player, maybe a little sharper than some of the other players that we had,” he said. “But I think once he touched the pitch and started playing, it was like, ‘Wait a minute.’ “Once I saw him, it was like, ‘Man, this is a different level than what I have and this is going to be fun.’ “To watch Diomandé play, it was just different in every way. I was very excited to have that opportunity and for the boys around him to be able to play with him because it was a considerable difference from the others.” Finding a new family Under Eason’s tutelage, Diomandé continued to develop not only as a player but as a person. But being away from his family wasn’t easy, especially in an industry that sometimes treats young players as cash cows. Instead of speaking only about the Beautiful Game, Eason would talk to Diomandé about his mother, who suffers from long-term health issues, and genuinely cared about the person behind the player. “He always wanted to get to the point where he could provide for his family and get his mom into hospitals to treat her,” Eason said. “I don’t think he’s driven by winning the Champions League; that’s a bonus, but he just wants to be playing at the highest level to be able to provide for his family and his friends.” Diomandé’s time at DME Academy ended in 2024, but he had already been invited to trials at professional clubs around the world. For several reasons, each would end up unsuccessful until a familiar agency got back involved. Ever since Diomandé had impressed scouts in Africa, he was being closely tracked and guided by American sports organization Blue Crow, which had invested in several professional teams across Europe. One of those teams at the time was Club Deportivo Leganés, which played in Spain’s top division, La Liga, at the time. With a keen interest in the African market, the club was tipped off about Diomandé at an early age and followed his progress in the US, eventually signing him in November 2024. The move was managed by Blue Crow, which was keen to secure its financial interest in Diomandé amid all the rising interest. The teenager’s move to Spain initially saw him play in the Leganés academy, then the reserves and then quickly rise through the ranks to the first team. Turning professional The club’s general manager Martín Ortega still remembers watching Diomandé train for the first time with the senior squad. “He was the best,” Ortega told CNN Sports. “The first time he took the ball, it felt like you were watching something special. You know, it was something impressive, special, not common at all. “Even some of the players of the first squad, when training ended, came to us and said this player has to play with us.” Just days after that practice session, Diomandé was called into the squad to play none other than Real Madrid in the league. In the 85th minute, the young winger made his professional debut as a late substitute. Although his team lost the match 3-2, his cameo was enough to prove he belonged at that level. “The first time he touched the ball, he dribbled to Federico Valverde as if he wasn’t a special player,” Ortega said. “He made an impressive match, and well, he helped us a lot at the end of that season. He played 10 matches and was the best, he was very impressive.” Suffering total heartbreak But in that same year where things were finally taking off, Diomandé experienced true heartbreak. While away from home, he received a message that his sister, Roxane, had died after her drink was spiked at a party. “Everything I do on a football pitch, it’s for you,” Diomandé recently wrote in an emotional open letter to his sister and biggest supporter. “I don’t even look at it like a game. I look at it like a stage. This is my chance to show the whole world what you saw in me. Every time I score, I’ll make sure everybody knows your name. I’ll make sure they don’t forget you.” Roxane was one of the people in his life who truly wanted the best for him. Her death became another motivational factor in Diomandé’s meteoric rise through the sport. On the pitch, the cat was out of the bag. Everyone could see what sort of talent the Ivorian winger was. Leganés tried to increase his release clause, but the bids were already coming in for him. Eventually, a deal was made with German club RB Leipzig and a clause put into the package that meant Leganés would get a cut from any future sale. At that point, the Spanish club was confident he would soon be snapped up by one of the game’s giants for mega money, so was happy to play the long game. “We knew what we had at home because we were watching him every training session. We knew that the player was special,” Ortega said. “He reminds me of (Barcelona and Spain superstar) Lamine Yamal because of the way he’s able to drive, you know, to make it look so easy. It’s because he makes it easy and it’s so natural.” One season excelling in Leipzig, as well as a brilliant showing at this summer’s World Cup, was enough to convince the top teams to start battling for his signature. Move to the Spanish capital Real Madrid, though, was not to be beaten and saw off several complications to finalize a deal. A lot of the issues revolved around who exactly represented Diomandé at different times of his career, with legal cases slowing down proceedings. Several people from his past saw the move to the 15-time Champions League winner as an opportunity to cash in on a player that they always saw as more of a commodity – sadly something which is all too common in soccer and sometimes leads to young players not fulfilling their true potential. But those who know Diomandé best told CNN Sports that it’s always been about the game for him, not the stuffy suits in boardrooms trying to squeeze out every penny. Given the money paid for him and the talent he has, it’s easy to forget the player is still only a teenager. Just three years ago he was playing youth soccer in the US; now, he’s a global star. Despite moving on from the DME Academy, Eason still maintains a relationship with his former pupil and attempts to help him navigate the often treacherous industry. Eason acknowledges that all the agents and representatives from his past could have easily derailed Diomandé’s career, but in the end, it was the Ivorian’s pure talent that rose above everything else. Joining Los Merengues will now pose the biggest test of his career. The scrutiny at the club is like no other, the media attention can be smothering and the level expected from fans is so high. The winger will be under the guidance of legendary manager José Mourinho, who is an ambassador of African talent (Didier Drogba, Samuel Eto’o, Mikel John Obi and Michael Essien among others) but who is as cutthroat as anyone. But Eason, who last spoke to Diomandé when he was in the US for the World Cup, said he doesn’t have any doubts the 19-year-old can rise to the challenge. “My passion for our relationship is making sure he’s just prepared as a young man to handle what is about to hit him,” Eason said. “The one thing that I don’t think a lot of people really notice is just how competitive he is. “I don’t know where his ceiling is. I’ve never seen him be overly challenged, so I’m excited to see him with Real. He might not be listed on paper as one of the top three players, but I have a feeling he’s going to work his way into that pretty quickly.”

articles.title: Australian Hussey open to Ashes Test role as England make approach
articles.summary: Ex-Australia batter Hussey said he was informally approached by Stephen Flemming, England’s new red-ball coach.
articles.body:
Australian great Mike Hussey could face his own country in the Ashes after saying he was open to joining England as their Test batting coach.

England host Australia in the Ashes in June, July and August next year, looking to take possession of the urn for the first time since 2015.

list 3 of 4 Infantino has ‘no way out’ as regional bodies consider no-confidence vote

list 4 of 4 James Harden agrees to three-year, $97m Cleveland Cavaliers deal: Report

Hussey has had an informal approach from England’s new red-ball coach Stephen Fleming, the duo having spent 15 years as teammates and then coaches at Indian Premier League side Chennai Super Kings.

“We obviously get on really well and work a lot together,” former Test stalwart Hussey told Fox Sports, where he is employed as a commentator.

“So it was just a bit of a passing comment, really saying, ‘Look, what do you reckon? Would you think about being the batting coach?'”

Hussey, known as “Mr Cricket” for his technical expertise, has just returned home after coaching Welsh Fire in The Hundred and said he had not given it proper consideration yet.

“To be honest, I have not been able to give it any thought whatsoever,” he said.

“Would I? I mean, I wouldn’t say never to anything really. I just love the coaching side of the game, and just to be able to work with different players.”

Should Hussey accept, it could see him plotting the downfall of Australia with Fleming when they tour England for the Ashes series next year.

Hussey admitted it would “feel a bit weird”.

“I have worked with England once before at the T20 World Cup (in 2022), and I must admit it did feel very weird pulling on that training shirt for the first time,” he said.

“But once you get in the nets and you start working with players, you sort of almost forget what shirt you’ve got on.

“So, look, I haven’t fully considered anything at this stage. I’m sort of just trying to take a bit of a break from it all at the moment and will give it some thought in due course.”

Fleming was appointed coach in late July following the sacking of fellow New Zealander Brendon McCullum, who remains in charge of England’s white-ball teams.

articles.title: Swiatek into Cincinnati semis after Rybakina injury
articles.summary: Elena Rybakina’s Cincinnati withdrawal raises concerns over the fitness of the world number two ahead of US Open.
articles.body:
Iga Swiatek moved into the semifinals of the ATP-WTA Cincinnati Masters as Elena Rybakina was forced to retire with a heel injury less than half an hour into their clash on Thursday.

Rybakina’s withdrawal raised concerns over the fitness of the world number two Kazakh just 10 days before the start of the US Open.

Trailing 4-1 in the opening set of Thursday’s Cincinnati quarterfinal, Rybakina suddenly pulled up short at 40-all, heading to her bench and consulting with the trainer.

She went back out and played one more point before quitting.

“I was feeling anxious watching the whole situation,” said her opponent Swiatek. “I hope she will be fine. Health is always the priority.

“This is an important tournament, but the US Open is the US Open. I hope she is ready for that,” she said, referring to the major which begins in New York on August 30.

“It was a shame she was injured, we were having a good match.”

Had two-time Grand Slam winner Rybakina reached the Cincinnati final, she would have risen to number one in the world for the first time in her career, following incumbent Aryna Sabalenka’s shock exit to 20-year-old Sara Bejlek.

Defending Cincinnati champion Swiatek said she had “gained a lot of confidence in the last weeks,” which have also included her victory over Rybakina in the final of this month’s Toronto event.

“I feel great, ready to play my game … I’m happy to be playing the tennis that I am.”

Poland’s Swiatek now plays a semifinal against Jessica Pegula, who is reportedly carrying a hip niggle after defeating Amanda Anisimova 6-2, 4-6, 7-6 (7/4).

Sixth-seeded Anisimova converted all five of her break points against Pegula, breaking her three times in the second set, before the world number three rebounded to win.

Pegula is setting WTA records at age 32. She is the fourth player since 2009 to reach five or more Masters 1000 quarterfinals after turning 30, along with Li Na, Serena Williams and Svetlana Kuznetsova.

Pegula needed just 34 minutes to pocket the opening set.

But Anisimova struck back in the second, earning a double break for 4-0.

After Anisimova squared the match at one set each, Pegula regrouped with an opening break in the deciding set.

They would each be broken twice as they went to the tiebreaker, where Pegula sealed the win on her first match point.

Pegula’s win was her sixth without a loss to Anisimova.

“I know I have a good record against her, but literally every single match is like it was today,” she said.

In the men’s draw, Flavio Cobolli advanced to the final four with a 2-6, 6-3, 6-4 defeat of Tommy Paul, gobbling down a handful of sweets for an unorthodox boost midway through the match.

The Roland Garros runner-up asked for the candy to be brought to the court and seemingly took energy from the pause before dispatching Paul, who had himself eliminated top seed Alexander Zverev 24 hours earlier.

“A sweet with chocolate makes me happy,” Cobolli said. “I’ve tried it in doubles so why not singles?”

Cobolli mounted the comeback after dropping the opening set.

With the match tied at a set apiece, Paul needed an extraordinary effort to hold serve for 4-3 in the final set, battling through five deuces and saving four break points.

But Cobolli ignored the showing and closed out the victory.

“It was a difficult day,” the winner said. “I’m proud of my effort, my game and my mental strength. It is all good practice for the US Open.

Cobelli will play for a place in the final when he faces Arthur Fils, who defeated Thiago Tirante 6-3, 6-2 in just 64 minutes — the shortest men’s match of the event.

Fils, the eighth Frenchman to reach Cincinnati semi-finals in the Open Era, said he was impressed by the weight of his opponent’s big game.

“He has an unbelievable serve; I was surprised by the speed of his ball,” he said.

“I tried to make him play a bit more. I stayed solid in my head and it worked pretty well for me.”

articles.title: CM Punk vs. Kevin Owens Preview and Prediction For WWE Championship Match on SmackDown
articles.summary: Kevin Owens vs. CM Punk is the shot in the arm WWE SmackDown needed to reinvigorate its main event scene.
articles.body:
Kevin Owens vs. CM Punk is the shot in the arm WWE SmackDown needed to reinvigorate its main event scene.

The blue brand has been a bit of a slog to watch since WrestleMania season. Cody Rhodes has been a remarkable champion over the last two years, but his storylines have mostly grown stale or overwrought.

Even his highly anticipated feud with Randy Orton wasn't enough to improve his current standing. Their latest interactions have been much better, without Pat McAfee involved to distract from their storied history together.

Conversely, Punk's jump to Friday nights has been a net positive for the brand. His long-awaited encounter with Rhodes at SummerSlam didn't quite live up to expectations, but the weekly segments were worth the price of admission.

Now, The Second City Saint must face an opponent from his past on his home turf, making for a must-see television matchup on SmackDown.

Owens' return from a 17-month hiatus was one of the highlights of SummerSlam weekend. More to the point, his victory at the two-night event set the stage for a match many have salivated over since Punk returned to WWE.

It's no secret that these two men don't like each other. Their brief backstage exchange in December 2023 was enough to leave us clamoring for more. They crossed paths again on Jan 31, 2025, but the gloves came off during their latest war of words.

Punk and Owens referenced their infamous 2006 confrontation in the Ring of Honor locker room and the T-shirt that sparked it. Even more, The Prizefighter took jabs at his performative grandstanding, proclivity for burning bridges, and the way he treated his friends.

Obviously, this could refer to Punk's highly publicized altercation with The Elite—Kenny Omega and The Young Bucks. However, you would have to be specific, as the Chicago native bristled because Owens is also friends with Colt Cabana and others.

This worked so well because it plays up what we know about Punk's time with All Elite Wrestling and what we don't know about lingering animosity his current colleagues may have toward him. That didn't feel like a typical wrestling promo.

Their tension was believable, and it made for the best segments of the year.

Yes, we've seen other heated rivalries where someone expressed how much they despise Punk. However, this one wasn't merely based on his first stint with WWE or the seven years he spent away from wrestling.

His feud with Owens feels deeply personal. Even more, the Canadian wrestler excels at breaking the fourth wall and exposing another side of the top protagonists. That's also what made his storyline with Rhodes so good back in 2024.

KO is also the perfect avatar for anyone with grievances about how Punk's post-WWE run went because he's not just a WWE guy. He's famously worked with indie promotions like PWG, CZW, and ROH, and he's a part of the same friend group that founded and inspired AEW.

That makes his barbs feel genuine. These aren't just scripted lines from someone with no connection to that part of the industry. His words are more impactful because, under different circumstances, Owens could've shared a locker room with The Elite.

Even if you believe Sami Zayn didn't get a fair shake as champion, that makes it so easy to root for his longtime friend. It's hard to imagine WWE would fully invest in a Punk heel turn in response to the online outrage over his latest world title win.

The undisputed champion is too popular right now to justify it. Still, his upcoming match in Toronto has allowed him to play a more antagonistic role against such a relatable underdog in his home country.

Expect Zayn to take matters into his own hands and get involved in this match. After all, Randy Orton instigated a brawl with Rhodes to close last week's episode, costing him a shot at the winner.

No matter how close Owens gets to his first world title win in 10 years, it's a safe bet that Zayn will interfere. It's plausible that the two could team up again to end Punk's reign, but we're betting he will actually play spoiler.

It makes much more sense for the champion to retain and keep this feud going. Owens and Zayn are also likely to remain in the mix for the upcoming men's Money in the Bank ladder match.

Considering his claims of conspiracies to keep him out of the title picture, Zayn has the most well-established motives to attain the briefcase. So, Punk is our pick to win, but he'll have an even bigger target ahead of the next premium live event.

articles.title: ‘It’s all I do’: Inside the year-long grind of the man behind college football’s Bible
articles.summary: Phil Steele is stumped. A man who spits out information for a living, who can recite chapter and verse on the offensive line at UMass, has no answer to an innocuous ice breaker of a question.
articles.body: Phil Steele is stumped. A man who spits out information for a living, who can recite chapter and verse on the offensive line at UMass, has no answer to an innocuous ice breaker of a question. He hems and haws for a few seconds before he finally gives up, admitting that he not only doesn’t have a favorite TV show; he can’t really name any. “I check the weather. I watch the news first thing in the morning,” he tells CNN Sports. “If my daughter wants to watch a movie, I’ll watch a movie.” Because, of course, Phil Steele doesn’t have time to binge-watch some Netflix or Hulu nonsense. He’s too busy consuming his daily dose of pigskin. The author of the veritable college football Bible – the eponymous “College Football Preview” – Steele long ago ditched such banalities as hobbies and pastimes. He watches college football. He rewatches college football. He takes notes on college football. He talks to coaches about college football. He writes about college football. He edits what he’s written about college football. He publishes a magazine about college football. Every year for the past 32 years, this is his livelihood and his life, his devotion to his craft so singular that only last summer did he finally see Europe for the first time. In return, Steele has carved a unique and profitable niche in the oversaturated American sports landscape by providing the two things fans crave most: information about their teams and the chance to sound smart. His is one of the few publications where the tagline – The Book Experts Cannot Do Without – isn’t hyperbole. Reporters and athletic administrators are among his most devoted buyers and coaches happily take his calls each year. The magazine’s arrival each year evokes the same giddiness kids once experienced when the Sears catalog popped in the mailbox around Christmas time, largely because it delivers the same sort of promise. College football can’t be far away. ‘It’s my world’ In 1992, Steele bought a six-acre property from the former wrestling coach at Saint Edward’s High School. The coach intended to use the barn as a wrestling room for his players. Steele has turned it into his rec room. There’s a trampoline, bikes and a full basketball court. Every day, along with hopping on his Peloton and ensuring he reaches his 15,000-step allotment, the proud papa of pigskin prognostications … hoops. It’s about the only time Steele isn’t watching or thinking or writing about football. “College football,” he says, “is all I do. It’s my world.” He came by his passion for pigskin honestly, through the pure-eyed adoration of childhood. Born in Cleveland, he rooted for his NFL (Browns) and college (Ohio State) hometown heroes, ravenously devouring the daily newspaper for information on his teams. His devotion changed when his father, Henry, introduced him to parlay cards – the pencil and paper betting sheets where picking multiple winners meant a nice little payout. A self-avowed math guy – “Don’t ask me about art,” he says. “I can’t even draw a stick figure” – Steele loved the challenge of studying and picking the winners in exchange for a few bucks. By 10, he was picking a steady stream of winners and crafting power rankings for his own enjoyment. Steele tried college, but nothing academic suited him quite like his love for football. At 21, he decided to bet on himself, quite literally, starting his own handicapping service. As Steele nuanced his skills, the service begat a newsletter – “Power Sweep” – crafted after his parents took out a second mortgage so he could buy a print shop. The first seven years he hemorrhaged money, his picks not nearly good enough to earn him a salary. Steele slept in the print shop, unsure what to do next. And then in 1989, the same year his father died of cancer, Steele went 53-23, the roll continuing through the next season. His handicapping merited attention and newsletter sales, but Steele soon tired of tipping his own hand to the oddsmakers in Vegas. “My underdog pick would start as a seven-point underdog, but then I’d put the information out and they’d be a four-point favorite,” he tells CNN Sports. “My picks lost value.” By the mid 1990s, the magazine section of the local bookstores and pharmacies were stuffed with football preview issues. Street & Smith’s was the originator, printing its first preview yearbook in 1940, but as the sport exploded, so did the market. Sporting News, Athlon and Lindy’s all crafted similar mags. Steele perused them on the regular, looking to pad his newsletter. Instead, he felt like he had more than they offered. The first “Phil Steele College Football Preview” was born in 1994. With 195 pages printed on black-and-white newsprint, it looked more like a beefed-up Daily Racing Form than a slick publication. Steele mailed it out to radio stations across the country, hoping they’d make a mention on air. “I had no idea what I was getting into,” he says. “Pretty soon, people needed the magazine. We stopped giving it out for free.” The making of the college football Bible The most recent issue of the magazine is a robust 375 pages and includes the same dense two-page spread for the Texas-San Antonio Roadrunners as it does for the Texas Longhorns. Every single FBS team – all 138 – is covered. It is not, by any stretch, literature, nor does it follow any sort of editorial style. Capitalizations show up at their leisure (Offense, Defense and Forecast) and some sentences require translation – Baylor 3-2 ATS L/5 vs FCS/under hit 3 str., for example. For spacing purposes, Steele has removed the following words – left, at, by, went, had, in, the, to, for, and, then and got – and has crafted his own abbreviations. DNR, in Steele’s case, is far less dire; it merely means a player did not return. The author – though Steele has a staff of around 10, he writes every word in every single two-page spread on every single team – makes no apologies. This is not a publication meant to meander through; it exists to provide information. There is an entire page devoted to NCAA experience, with an explanation of his formula used to rank teams and a two-page spread to cover the results of every single bowl game for the last 10 years. On the team pages, there are paragraphs devoted to every position, forecasts for both sides of the ball, nuggets to help set the stage for each game, and the past five years’ results, complete with the line. Not to mention predictions for the country’s top individual units, surprise teams (last year, it was Oklahoma, which went from 6-7 to the playoff; this year, it’s Alabama) and most importantly, his preseason top 40 and conference orders of finish. “My goal is to be graded as the most accurate magazine,” Steele said. “And I should be. Nobody puts the time into it that I do.” He is not exaggerating. Steele is a man of routine and excess preparation. He wakes each morning at 5:45, hops on his Peloton and watches one of two things – either an old game on tape or a replay of SportsCenter. If it’s the latter, he condenses the show into minutes, skipping through anything that doesn’t have to do with college football. After that, he heads to his office. On a college football Saturday, he will arrive by 7 in the morning and by noon has his bank of TVs cued up, 12 games running simultaneously. He’ll do the same for the 4 p.m. kickoffs before heading home for the night games, where he cuts back. Steele only watches eight games at once then. He gets by on a steady diet of caffeine, his self-deprecating “see-food” diet (“If I see it, I eat it,” he says) and an obsessive addiction to college football. It is impossible to see every play of every game, but the downtime in between allows Steele to scan back and forth. He takes copious notes on what he sees, crafting notebooks full of information and also creates and tracks nine sets of power rankings on a computer spreadsheet that, to the untrained eye, looks like color-coded gibberish. To Steele, it makes perfect sense. The portal has made his work harder, not just in terms of gathering information but getting a handle on whether a roster will and won’t mesh, but if he has a pet peeve, it’s the revolving closet of uniforms. “Sometimes, it takes me until halfway through the first quarter to figure out who someone is,” he said. A year-long passion project When the games stop, Steele continues. During the course of the season, he has a service that provides every article written about every team and when there are no longer games to watch, he reads. He’s looking for trends and progressions at various positions, subtle shifts he might otherwise miss in his game watching. Some schools might generate only a handful of print; a team like Ohio State, on the other hand, produces its own anthology. In the spring, he starts calling around to coaches. As the magazine’s popularity grew, so, too, did Steele’s reputation. Conferences started to invite him to speak at their media days, where he earned introductions to the men who headed up the teams he wrote about. For this year’s issue, Steele spoke to 133 of the 138 teams featured. It all coalesces through three edits and iterations into the one-of-a-kind magazine that comes out in July. Or Steele thought it was one of a kind. This year, a customer called Steele’s office to complain about the smaller book he purchased online. “We don’t have a smaller book, for crying out loud,” Steele says. A quick search revealed the culprit: Four fakes for sale on Amazon. A furious Steele posted a lengthy buyer beware warning on both his website and X, apoplectic that someone would steal his name and minimize his life’s work. Told that imitation is the highest form of flattery, Steele guffaws. “Not in this case,” he says. “They put my name on an inferior product.” The irony is not lost on Steele that what began as a passion project has, in some ways, altered his passion. Though his daughter is a nursing student at Ohio State, Steele is no longer a Buckeye devotee. His definition of a favorite team is the underdog he picked higher than everyone else. And while he devours more college football than ever before, the kid who once watched wide-eyed at his heroes can no longer watch a game without a clinical, detached assessment. “I’ll be in the barn watching UL-Monroe against Georgia State and I’m thinking about next year’s magazine,” he says. “Like how does the offensive line look?” But it does get him thinking, back to the original icebreaker question. Steele does, he realizes, watch a little TV for entertainment. “I like to watch FCS football,” he says. “I have nothing on it. Don’t have to make a pick. I can just sit back and watch.”

articles.title: Fury says fight with Joshua looks unlikely with venue yet to be agreed
articles.summary: The all-British, much anticipated boxing showdown between Fury and Joshua was scheduled for November.
articles.body:
Former world heavyweight champion Tyson ⁠⁠Fury has said his long-awaited boxing showdown with fellow Briton Anthony Joshua “doesn’t look like it’s going to happen”, accusing his rival and promoter Eddie Hearn of being “money-thirsty”.

The Joshua vs Fury fight – one of the biggest in British boxing history – was expected to be held in November after both signed a contract with Turki Alalshikh, Saudi Arabia’s General Entertainment Authority chairman.

“Doesn’t look like they’re going to sign the fight, and it doesn’t look like it’s going to happen all because Eddie Hearn and that want more money,” Fury said in a series of expletive-laden Instagram stories on Friday.

According to several media reports, Joshua and his promoter Hearn have signed a contract for the fight to be staged in the United Kingdom, while Saudi organisers are pushing for a move to the United States, with Madison Square Garden in New York emerging as the frontrunner.

Fury, the two-time world champion, said Joshua is demanding a bigger fight purse.

“They have already had that much money off Turki [Alalshikh] over the last few years, Eddie and AJ, they have had boxing deals, they have had darts deals, they have had snooker deals, they have had everything,” Fury added.

“And yet, they have got the audacity … to ask for more money from old Turki that you have had combined over the last couple of years.”

Calling Joshua and Hearn “disgusting”, Fury added that he would move on and fight someone else.

“… But just know you never had the guts to fight Tyson Fury, ever, you little coward,” he said.

Fury, who ⁠⁠turns 38 in August, has won 36 ⁠⁠professional bouts, suffering his ⁠⁠only losses in two fights with Ukraine’s Oleksandr Usyk in 2024. He announced his return to boxing in January, having retired from the sport in December 2024 after losing to Usyk in a bout for three of the four major world titles.

Joshua and Fury were unable to agree on terms in 2021, and plans for the face-off fell apart after a US judge ruled Fury had to face Deontay Wilder in a trilogy fight instead.

articles.title: Mikey Lewis: Hull KR coach Willie Peters explains decision to drop star half-back ahead of two-match ban
articles.summary: Willie Peters chose not to include Mikey Lewis in his squad for Saturday's match against Toulouse as Hull KR look to 'uphold standards'; round 24 of Super League continues on Friday August 21, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Lewis copped a two-game ban after a Grade C charge for 'dangerous contact' with Warrington Wolves' Ewan Irwin during their rearranged round two fixture on Tuesday.

Lewis' studs hit the ankle of Irwin as he kicked the ball. Irwin is now an injury worry for Sam Burgess' side and is undergoing scans.

The ban comes just as the 25-year-old returned from a four-match ban for a headbutt the last time the Robins faced Warrington.

Tevita Pangai Jr also faces a four-match ban after being cited three times during the match for 'late contact with a passer'. It means his Robins career could now be over after signing for them mid-season.

Although the disciplinary review has already taken place, the bans will only come into effect for Round 25, meaning both players were available for Saturday's clash with Toulouse.

However, Peters opted against including either player in his squad due to having to "uphold standards" not just for now, but for the club moving forward and making sure there is a clear line of what they will "accept" no matter "who you are".

That means the earliest Lewis will return is the final round of the regular season.

"It's noted that we're the most charged team in the competition in terms of disciplinary points," Peters said.

"We have been given the most points out of any other team in the competition and had the most players sitting on the sideline.

"Some players have done things without consequence and if you don't have consequence, then you keep repeating those actions.

"So it's a time that we made a decision that it's not acceptable to be sitting on the sideline and costing team-mates through behaviours that's not in line with our standards.

"There's times there where it's not deliberate or there's no malice, but when there's repeated efforts, we've made a decision to not play those two this week and, as I said, it's more around our standards, what we're going to accept or what we're not going to accept.

"I believe it will help us, hopefully this year, but more importantly, it will help the club going forward that there's a standard that we want to uphold and if we're not upholding that and no matter who you are, then there needs to be consequence and that's what we've chosen to do."

While Peters made clear that he needs his players to accept the consequences of their actions, he admits Hull KR are a better outfit with Lewis in the team, but more particularly when he is "in line".

"We are a better team, obviously, with Mikey Lewis in it and we've shown that over the years.

"Mikey, I thought for the majority of the game had a lot of positive actions and it was his first game back and I thought he, as I said before, had a strong impact in the way he defended.

"But there is certain things that he needs to improve and he's aware of that. We all keep conversations between us, but we're certainly supportive of Mikey and we want to improve Mikey in certain areas of the game that he needs to and he's aware of that.

"He is obviously going to have sit a few weeks on the sidelines, and we'll see where it goes. But as I said, we're a better team with Mikey Lewis in it and when he is in line with the standards everyone wants to uphold."

articles.title: Australian Darts Masters: James Wade dominates tournament opener as Ross Smith stunned by Brody Klinge in Wollongong
articles.summary: James Wade thrashed Tim Pusey 6-0 in the opening round of the Australian Darts Masters; Gian van Veen, Stephen Bunting, Josh Rock, Jonny Clayton and Gerwyn Price all made winning starts as Ross Smith made a shock early exit
articles.body:
Klinge was the solitary Oceanic representative to triumph on a terrific opening day at the WIN Entertainment Centre, registering an 11-dart break to sink Ross Smith in a deciding-leg epic.

Smith crashed in eight maximums during a captivating affair, although he was punished for squandering two match darts in the decider, as Klinge celebrated the biggest victory of his career.

"I'm over the moon with that," said Klinge, who averaged 96 to Smith's 102.88. "That was the adrenaline rush of my life. I felt a lot more comfortable playing this time around and it showed in my performance I think.

"Ross was throwing everything at me. I was lucky he missed at the end there, but I took my chance. I'm on a free rein now. I'm just going to do my best and keep going. There's no pressure on me."

Klinge's reward is a tussle against Van Veen on Finals Day, after the world No 2 conjured up a spectacular 161 checkout to wrap up a clinical 6-3 success against Raymond Smith.

However, the performance of the night was produced by James Wade, who averaged 112.73 - the second-highest recorded in a World Series of Darts event in Australia - during a six-leg demolition of Tim Pusey.

"That felt amazing. Everything just fell into my hands there," admitted Wade, who closed out victory with a 164 finish and will play Stephen Bunting in the quarter-finals.

"I think I'm guilty of sometimes forgetting how lucky I am to do what I do, but I'm just happy to be here and I'm playing alright. If I replicate that level tomorrow everyone is stuffed, but tomorrow is a different day!"

2024 champion Gerwyn Price will face Josh Rock in a fascinating last-eight showdown on Saturday, having reeled off four consecutive legs - including back-to-back 124 and 108 checkouts - in a 6-2 victory over Simon Whitlock.

Rock also won four straight legs to seal a 6-3 success against Adam Leek, while Jonny Clayton will go head-to-head with Australian No 1 Damon Heta after opening his bid for back-to-back World Series titles with a hard-fought 6-3 victory against Ben Robb.

Heta averaged 102.39 in his 6-2 thumping of fellow countryman Joe Comito, while the other tie saw Stephen Bunting fight back from trailing 3-0 to beat Mal Cuming 6-3.

articles.title: Freedom 250 Continues The History Of DC Races Celebrating America's Birthday
articles.summary: Exactly 225 years after Thomas Jefferson celebrated America's birthday with a horse race, the Freedom 250 is taking over D.C.
articles.body: The Freedom 250 isn't the first race hosted in Washington, D.C. by the U.S. president in celebration of America's birthday.  On July 4th, 1801, 225 years ago, to celebrate America's 25th birthday, President Thomas Jefferson helped put on festivities including horseback riding and cockfighting in Washington, D.C., according to the White House Historical Association.  Jefferson, the third President of the United States, and the Washington Jockey Club "established a racecourse just blocks from the White House, with part of the course running across Pennsylvania Avenue and through what is now Lafayette Park." According to the White House Historical Association, "the north grounds of the President's Park came alive at daybreak with the raising of tents and booths, soon followed by crowds of people. A festival took place just for the day. Food and drink and cottage goods of all types were sold. There were horse races and parades of the Washington Militia, along with other military companies.  After the festivities, Jefferson invited attendees into the White House. The tradition of an annual reception at the White House continued for much of the nineteenth century. Not only did Jefferson host a horse race near the White House, but he was an avid supporter and participant in horse racing. He often attended meets at the National Race Course in Washington, D.C. Now Donald J. Trump, the 47th president of the U.S., is helping to bring a 250-mile, 147-lap race to Washington, D.C. to celebrate America's 250th birthday.  "I'm thrilled to be here with some of the most extraordinary figures in the history of motorsports and any sport, if you think about it," Trump said at a Freedom 250 Grand Prix Showcase on July 13. "As we count down to the Freedom 250 Grand Prix, this will be like no other race, ever. I don't think anything will ever be — will ever top what we're going to be having." The Freedom 250 Grand Prix of Washington, D.C., is the first INDYCAR race ever held in the nation's capital. The FOX pre-race show will begin at 11:30 a.m. ET on Sunday, Aug. 23, with the green flag scheduled for 1:13 p.m. ET. The course does not reach the White House, but it runs along Pennsylvania Avenue, Constitution Avenue and in front of the Washington Monument.  The Freedom 250 Grand Prix is the second event hosted in proximity to the White House this summer, along with UFC Freedom 250.  With this being the initial INDYCAR race in Washington, D.C., no drivers have course experience as an upper hand. But Alex Palou (542 points) enters Sunday's race with a healthy lead in the standings, despite finishing fourth at the Ontario Honda Dealers Indy at Markham last Sunday.  The battle for second place is much closer, with Kyle Kirkwood (409), David Malukas (405) and Christian Lundgaard (403) separated by six points. So while the Freedom 250 will be a spectacle to watch, INDYCAR's top drivers can't lose focus as the stakes are high. articles.body:
England crushed ‌Pakistan by an innings and 103 runs to win a one-sided first Test at Headingley and ⁠launch Joe Root’s second ⁠spell as permanent captain in style.

The convulsions which accompanied the series defeat by New Zealand eight weeks ago, with Ben Stokes stepping down and coach Brendon McCullum being relieved of ⁠his red-ball duties, were emphatically put behind them by England.

A dominant display against a hugely disappointing Pakistan side saw the game wrapped up before tea on Friday on the third day, despite the loss of more than ⁠half a day’s play to rain.

After England added 43 runs to their overnight score to reach 409 and gain a first innings lead of 238, their pace attack routed the tourists. Mohammad Rizwan top scored with 41 as Pakistan were bowled out for 135 in 37.3 overs.

England’s Josh Tongue, who was playing in The Hundred season’s final ‌three days before the start of the test match, finished with 3-43 and Ollie Robinson 3-29. Their match figures of 8-89 and 8-80 respectively were test-career bests.

For the second time in the match, Pakistan lost their first wicket without a run on the board as Imam-ul-Haq gloved Jofra Archer to wicketkeeper Jamie Smith in the second over and it was something of a procession thereafter.

In Archer’s second over, Azan Awais was caught at leg slip by Root, who had just moved himself there in a prescient ⁠piece of captaincy. It was Root’s 219th test catch, taking him back ahead ⁠of Australia’s Steve Smith atop the all-time non-wicketkeeper list.

Everything Root touched turned to gold with Saud Shakeel clipping Tongue to an unusual backward square leg position where Dan Lawrence took a fine diving catch.

When Shan Masood went for 29 from 56 balls, edging Tongue ⁠to Ben Duckett at slip, the Nottinghamshire quick was on a hat-trick for the second time in the match.

Salman Ali Agha foiled the attempt but the Pakistan ⁠captain was trapped leg before wicket (lbw) later in the over.

Everything was going England’s ⁠way and when Ali Usman nicked Robinson into wicketkeeper Jamie Smith’s leg, the ball ricocheted into the diving Jamie Cox’s hands at slip.

Cox took another sharp catch off Robinson to remove Khurram Shahzad before Archer, who took 3-50, dismissed Mohammad Abbas to finish the match.

For Pakistan, ‌the shared series in the West Indies earlier this month was made to look like a false dawn.

The gulf between the penetration of the two sides’ seam attacks, the comfort of the two batting lineups in ‌English ‌conditions and their athleticism in the field was glaring.

The second test in the three-match series starts at Lord’s on Thursday when Pakistan will hope to have captain Babar Azam back after a finger injury.

articles.title: NHL Expects to Hold Outdoor Game in Europe In 'Relatively Near Future,' Deputy Commissioner Says
articles.summary: One day after announcing Germany will host four games during the 2027-28 regular season, the next step for the NHL appears to be getting Europe to host an outdoor game.
articles.body:
One day after announcing Germany will host four games during the 2027-28 regular season, the next step for the NHL appears to be getting Europe to host an outdoor game.

Speaking to Tom Gulitti of NHL.com, NHL deputy commissioner Bill Daly expressed with confidence the league will hold an outdoor game in a European market in the "relatively near future" though he couldn't provide a specific timeline.

"I think it's going to happen, for sure," Daly said. "When it's going to happen, I couldn't tell you, but I would say relatively near future would be a good guess."

The games in Germany will be divided between Munich and Cologne. The Boston Bruins will play twice at the SAP Garden in Munich, while the Edmonton Oilers will set up camp at Lanxess Arena in Cologne.

Based on the NHL's increased commitment to playing regular-season games overseas, an outdoor event at some point would be the logical next step.

Germany has hosted regular-season games dating back to the 2011-12 season. The Ottawa Senators and Chicago Blackhawks will play twice in Düsseldorf on Dec. 18 and 20.

Daly hinted at Allianz Arena, home of FC Bayern Munich, as a potential host venue for the outdoor game: "Yeah, I think that's fair."

It would make sense in the wake of the NHL and FC Bayern entering a multiyear partnership designed to help grow the sport of hockey in Germany and build Bayern's fanbase in North America.

Allianz Arena has a max capacity of 75,024 for soccer matches. Assuming a similar attendance for an NHL game, that would rank among the largest crowds in the history of the league.

The NHL Stadium Series, which began back in 2014, has featured 18 games and 19 teams. The most recent matchup at Raymond James Stadium saw the Tampa Bay Lightning defeat the Boston Bruins 6-5 in a shootout on Feb. 1.

AT&T Stadium is scheduled to host the next Stadium Series matchup on Feb. 1, 2027, between the Vegas Golden Knights and Dallas Stars.

The 2026-27 NHL regular season begins on Sept. 29 with the Florida Panthers taking on the defending Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes.

articles.title: WWE Rumors on Ilja Dragunov's Departure, John Cena Classic, Lola Vice Main Roster Call-Up
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.

Reported Details Behind Dragunov's WWE Exit

Ilja Dragunov's absence from WWE programming for four months prior to his departure was reportedly related to his contract status.

According to Dave Meltzer of the Wrestling Observer Newsletter (h/t WrestlePurists ), Dragunov had a "very good" contract with WWE, but the two sides were far enough apart in negotiations for a new deal that the decision was made to pull him from television in April.

Meltzer (h/t WrestlePurists) added that the disconnect between Dragunov and WWE had to do with the company's perception of Dragunov and how big of a draw he actually was.

WWE reportedly viewed Dragunov as a good in-ring performer, but not a "numbers mover," and the company reportedly felt he needed to be a numbers mover in order to justify the type of money he was asking for.

It was first reported by PWInsider.com (h/t WrestlePurists ) on Thursday that Dragunov's WWE contract was expiring, and he intended to leave the company.

Per False Finish , WWE "would have liked Dragunov to stay with the company," but Dragunov made the choice to leave.

Dragunov signed with WWE in 2019, and he went on to have success as a member of multiple brands. That included holding the NXT United Kingdom Championship, the NXT Championship and the United States Championship one time each.

His TV time on SmackDown took a hit after dropping the U.S. title to Carmelo Hayes in December, though, and after competing in the Andre the Giant Memorial Battle Royal in April, Dragunov was not seen again on WWE programming.

While a talent typically has a 90-day non-compete clause they have to adhere to when they are released by WWE, Dragunov's contract lapsed.

That means he is free to sign and work anywhere once his contract has officially expired, per Meltzer.

With AEW All In set for Wembley Stadium in London on Aug. 30, Dragunov could be a fun surprise entrant in the Casino Gauntlet match should he decide to sign with the promotion.

WWE Reportedly Considering Date for John Cena Classic

Although there are still plenty of questions regarding what the John Cena Classic will entail, WWE reportedly has a date in mind for the tournament.

According to False Finish , WWE is "currently looking at holding" the John Cena Classic on Saturday, Dec. 12, although the location isn't yet known.

The John Cena Classic concept was first announced by John Cena himself during the Backlash premium live event in May.

Cena divulged that it would be a tournament comprised of Superstars from both WWE's main roster and NXT. Cena added that a John Cena Classic champion would be crowned at the end based on a fan vote rather than the results of the matches.

That last point led to some confusion among fans, but the fact that WWE hasn't not followed up on Cena's announcement at all since May suggests that the company may still be trying to iron out the details.

Since Dec. 12 is a Saturday, that suggests the John Cena Classic will either be a standalone premium live event or part of a Saturday Night's Main Event should it happen on that date.

Every indication is that the John Cena Classic is meant to elevate up-and-coming stars and help them build a connection with the fans, which should only be a positive for WWE moving forward.

WWE Reportedly Preparing Vice for Main Roster Call-Up

WWE has reportedly set the wheels in motion for Lola Vice's main roster debut.

According to TRNBCKL (h/t False Finish ), vignettes featuring Vice have been filmed, and they are expected to air "in the coming weeks" leading up to her official call-up from NXT to the main roster.

A former MMA fighter with Bellator, Vice signed with WWE in 2022 and established herself as one of the top women's Superstars in NXT.

After vying for the title on multiple occasions, she finally won the NXT Women's Championship at Stand & Deliver in April, beating Jacy Jayne and Kendal Grey in a Triple Threat match.

Vice dropped the title to Grey less than three months later at Great American Bash, though, and Grey then defeated Vice in an NXT Underground match earlier this month.

That likely represented Vice's final NXT match, as she has been rumored for a call-up to the main roster for quite some time.

Bryan Alvarez of Wrestling Observer Radio (h/t Subhojeet Mukherjee of Ringside News) reported last month that SmackDown would likely be Vice's home on the main roster.

If that proves to be true, then vignettes for her debut could potentially start airing as soon as Friday night's episode of SmackDown.

articles.title: FIFA Suspends 3 Argentina Players A Combined 18 Games For World Cup Final Scuffle
articles.summary: FIFA on Friday handed bans to three Argentina players, led by a 10-match suspension for midfielder Leandro Paredes, for striking Spain opponents moments after the World Cup final.
articles.body: FIFA banned three Argentina players on Friday, including a 10-match suspension for midfielder Leandro Paredes, for striking Spain opponents after losing the World Cup final. The ban for Paredes — who grabbed Spain's Eric Garcia by the throat and pushed Gavi to the ground — ranks with the FIFA sanctions for Uruguay forward Luis Suarez in 2014 as among the most severe in World Cup history. Argentina defender Nahuel Molina was handed a seven-game ban while Thiago Almada was given a one-game suspension. FIFA imposed fines of $90,000 on Paredes and Molina, and $30,000 for Almada. The ban for Paredes is effectively a one-year expulsion from the Argentina team as the FIFA calendar for national team schedules includes 10 games through June 2027. All of those games could be friendlies with no competitive games currently scheduled. Spain's Gavi also banned for game vs England Gavi also was banned for one game, which is a Nations League match for Spain against England at Wembley on Sept. 26. An Argentina coach, Roberto Ayala, also got a three-game ban and $30,000 fine. The Argentine Football Association was fined $110,000 for a range of incidents during the World Cup including players carrying a political banner about the Falkland Islands after the semifinal win against England, and discriminatory chants by fans. AFA also was ordered by FIFA to spend $100,000 on anti-racism projects. Argentina received $34 million in World Cup prize money from FIFA. Argentina expected to appeal AFA can appeal the longer sanctions and fines to FIFA, and likely after at the Court of Arbitration for Sport. "The AFA legal department will, in a timely manner, request from FIFA the grounds for the reviewable rulings in order to file appeals with the governing body’s appeal committee, while retaining the future option of appealing to the CAS as a final recourse," the federation said in a statement. Suárez and Simunic cases In 2014, Suárez was banned from all soccer for four months, including for his new club Barcelona, and eight more competition games for Uruguay for biting Italy defender Giorgio Chiellini in a World Cup group stage game in Brazil. The on-field clashes at last month's final in East Rutherford, New Jersey — which were charged by FIFA as assault cases — came after Argentina lost a testy final to Spain where it was mostly outplayed and barely created a scoring chance.
